documents.excerpt: Stop trying to hide your sin as Isaiah did, diverting attention from his stuff by pointing his finger and clucking his tongue at yours. God knew, and still chose to use Isaiah anyway.
excerpts: Stop trying to hide your sin as Isaiah did, diverting attention from his stuff by pointing his finger and clucking his tongue at yours. God knew, and still chose to use Isaiah anyway.

It isn’t just “hate the sin, love the sinner.” God condemns our sin but loves us too much to call us sinners; he calls us back to himself. So he called a liar named Abraham his friend, a murderer named David a man after his own heart, and a lily-livered bowl of jelly named Peter the Rock. God sees us not as we are but as what we can become through him.

We will never live a nanosecond free from sin, and claiming otherwise claims equal status with God. We are fallen, broken people, but God loves people and chooses to work through them. In him Steve lives and moves and has his being, and yet he is overwhelmed that God has a need for him.

documents.excerpt: A man with an awful headache told his doctor he never touches liquor, thinks smoking is disgusting, and is in bed at 10:00 with his wife. Asked if it was a sharp, shooting pain, he said yes. The doctor’s diagnosis: “You have your halo on too tight. Let me loosen it some.”
excerpts: A man with an awful headache told his doctor he never touches liquor, thinks smoking is disgusting, and is in bed at 10:00 with his wife. Asked if it was a sharp, shooting pain, he said yes. The doctor’s diagnosis: “You have your halo on too tight. Let me loosen it some.”

Steve isn’t preaching a pro-sin message; Paul clearly said, “Shall we go on sinning so that grace may abound? By no means.” It’s a friendly reminder that you can be rabidly anti-sin and still full of sin, and not struggling where someone else struggles doesn’t mean you should apply for sainthood or try on halos at Target. If you think you deserve one, wear it loose and let it tilt, because we all have scabby lips and gimpy hips.

Get over your bad self. Your battles may differ from Steve’s, but take inventory: corpses strewn over your life, smoke billowing from moral, spiritual, and relational mishaps, loved ones discarded because they weren’t worthy or wouldn’t take the steps you thought they should. Forgetting the ravages of your own story is a spiritual peril. If you want God to use you with struggling, broken people, learn to lick your lips before you ever open your mouth.

excerpts: Very soon Isaiah will prophesy beautiful words about a virgin with child, named Immanuel, God with us, and a child to be born and a son given, called Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, and Prince of Peace.

But before the gospel can get that good, that same child would be despised and rejected, a man of sorrows familiar with suffering, pierced for our transgressions, crushed for our iniquities, the punishment that brought us peace placed on him. All of it to this end: that mercy could happen. Jesus would be punished so that people ravaged by sin, their own or others’, and people who are hurting, lonely, desperate, and can’t ever seem to get it right, could be welcomed in anyway, and grace extended anyway. documents.excerpt: If you don’t think you need mercy, you need a severe case of chapped lips. Only then will you realize people aren’t motivated to walk the path of righteousness by your rules, control, intimidation, and threats, but as you lift up Jesus, extend God’s love in massive doses, and trust the Holy Spirit alone to redirect their hearts. That’s what Isaiah the man needed to change about himself.

Before the wilderness: the baptism
Steve reminded the church a few weeks ago that before Jesus went out to live one of Chris’s worst nightmares, not eating for 40 days (“I like to eat”), he stopped to be baptized by John. Chris reads Matthew 3 from verse 13: John tried to deter him, Jesus said it was proper to fulfill all righteousness, heaven opened, the Spirit descended like a dove, and a voice said, “This is my Son, whom I love; with him I am well pleased.”
Chris is with John: “Excuse me, you want me to baptize you? Maybe it’s opposite day.” John knows who he is looking at; he has been preparing the way for him. Jesus says, in effect, “You heard right.” Then he is led by the Spirit into the wilderness, a place so terrible even the animals didn’t hang out there, where he fasts and is tempted by the devil.
documents.title: Before the wilderness: the baptism — Scripture: Your Defense

documents.context: Chris DeWald · November 24, 2024 · Temptation: The Temptations of Jesus
documents.excerpt: These 40 days are how Jesus prepared for his ministry. For 30 years he lived a quiet life as a carpenter; then his first stop was baptism and his second the wilderness. Chris believes the wilderness prepared him not because he needed it but because we did: everything Jesus did was for us. He was in heaven “living the dream,” but he came to die for us, live for us, and be an example for us. He was called, he prepared, then he began his ministry.

excerpts: These 40 days are one battle in the long war Satan has waged against God and his creation, and Satan has known Jesus since his creation. John 1: in the beginning was the Word, the Word was with God and was God, and through him all things were made. All, not some.

If someone says that means only the universe and not heavenly beings, Colossians 1 from verse 15 says the Son is the image of the invisible God, and in him all things were created, things in heaven and on earth, visible and invisible, thrones, powers, rulers, and authorities, and through him God reconciled all things by making peace through his blood shed on the cross. Chris rereads verse 16: there is nothing Jesus didn’t create.

That hits Chris at the core, because we want to put God in a box and say Jesus was just a man. Wrong. The only thing he didn’t create was God himself. Jesus knows Satan as one of his creations, and Satan knows Jesus as his creator.

The Lord pointed to his blameless servant Job; Satan said Job feared God only because of God’s hedge and blessing, and the Lord gave everything Job had into Satan’s power, but not the man himself.

Satan just moseys right into the presence of the Lord with the angels. If Chris were one of the other angels, he would have wanted to take a swing (“a big old uppercut”). Worse, Satan comes back again in chapter 2.

Satan was created by Jesus, and Job makes clear he has spent time before God’s throne. In the wilderness he isn’t a stranger; he knows Jesus’ power, which is why he tempts him to do miracles. Humans debate and reject that Jesus is God, but Satan knew exactly who Jesus was and wanted to dethrone him.

documents.excerpt: Satan twisted Scripture to deceive Jesus, and he does it to us, and we are more vulnerable than Jesus was. excerpts: Satan twisted Scripture to deceive Jesus, and he does it to us, and we are more vulnerable than Jesus was. Chris sometimes watches a Mormon apologist to understand how they interpret Scripture, and notices that no matter what the text says, he makes it fit, sometimes pulling out an obscure expert to define a Greek word in a way no one else does.

Satan is brilliant at taking truth and creating a lie close to it that sounds amazing and even seems to make sense, but if it’s not in God’s word, it’s false doctrine. Paul warned the Corinthians in 2 Corinthians 11 about false apostles masquerading as apostles of Christ: Satan himself masquerades as an angel of light, so his servants masquerade as servants of righteousness, set on deceiving the lost and the church.

But a brother or sister who brings an incorrect interpretation isn’t necessarily masquerading; they may just need a mature believer to help them. Provide love and correction, and don’t confuse them with someone trying to steer you wrong.

1. Scripture can be twisted to fit what someone wants
Satan twisted Scripture to deceive Jesus, and he does it to us, and we are more vulnerable than Jesus was. Chris sometimes watches a Mormon apologist to understand how they interpret Scripture, and notices that no matter what the text says, he makes it fit, sometimes pulling out an obscure expert to define a Greek word in a way no one else does.
Satan is brilliant at taking truth and creating a lie close to it that sounds amazing and even seems to make sense, but if it’s not in God’s word, it’s false doctrine. Paul warned the Corinthians in 2 Corinthians 11 about false apostles masquerading as apostles of Christ: Satan himself masquerades as an angel of light, so his servants masquerade as servants of righteousness, set on deceiving the lost and the church.
But a brother or sister who brings an incorrect interpretation isn’t necessarily masquerading; they may just need a mature believer to help them. Provide love and correction, and don’t confuse them with someone trying to steer you wrong.

He reads Hebrews 4: we have a great high priest who is able to empathize with our weaknesses, one who has been tempted in every way, just as we are, yet did not sin.
excerpts: Chris addresses a claim he has heard: that because Jesus was God in the flesh, he doesn’t really understand what we go through. He reads Hebrews 4: we have a great high priest who is able to empathize with our weaknesses, one who has been tempted in every way, just as we are, yet did not sin.

Everything the Bible tells us to do to defeat sin and temptation, flee, resist, take every thought captive, Jesus did himself; we know because he never sinned. Don’t ever tell Chris that Jesus doesn’t understand. You’re not alone; he has been through it.

More than that, he suffered more than we will ever know: the physical suffering leading to the cross and the cross itself, then taking on every sin humanity has ever committed or will commit, and experiencing what he had never known, being forsaken by his Father because of our sin. He cried out, “My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?” We have no way of understanding what he went through: the suffering, the pain, the rejection, the loneliness. “I don’t think I understand.”

documents.excerpt: About 1,991 years ago there was a 40-day showdown in the Judean desert between the kingdoms of this world and the kingdom of God: the world’s prince versus God’s Prince. Newspapers stopped writing about it, some churches stopped talking about it, and Christians rarely live in its power, but Josh’s heart pumps faster because of it, the church is unshakable in light of it, and eternity is visible as a result of it.
excerpts: About 1,991 years ago there was a 40-day showdown in the Judean desert between the kingdoms of this world and the kingdom of God: the world’s prince versus God’s Prince. Newspapers stopped writing about it, some churches stopped talking about it, and Christians rarely live in its power, but Josh’s heart pumps faster because of it, the church is unshakable in light of it, and eternity is visible as a result of it.

In the desert Jesus answered who has power over who, who will outlast, and who is the greatest, clinging to a kingdom that lasts forever and is infinitely more valuable than anything we can claim here on earth.

We are given three examples of the temptations, which can be read in five minutes and which the church has extended to a three-week series, but for Jesus this was 40 days. Luke and Matthew record them in a different order; Josh’s take is that it doesn’t matter, because the list isn’t exhaustive but a summary of 40 days, and for all we know Jesus was tempted many times.

documents.excerpt: Isn’t this how the devil works? Someone feels the Lord calling him to stop watching porn, to control his temper, or to stop pursuing material things, and Josh says that sounds like something the Lord would want. Then along comes the first temptation, and fresh from a sermon or a podcast you say, “No, get behind me, Satan.”
excerpts: Isn’t this how the devil works? Someone feels the Lord calling him to stop watching porn, to control his temper, or to stop pursuing material things, and Josh says that sounds like something the Lord would want. Then along comes the first temptation, and fresh from a sermon or a podcast you say, “No, get behind me, Satan.”

You honestly think that’s it? That the devil says, “Guess he’s changed, guess she’s turned over a new leaf,” and goes to find somebody else? The devil is like a birthmark: you might wish it wasn’t there, but it’s still there.

What Josh has learned clinging to Christ through multiple addictions and endless temptations: you don’t find victory by trying to suppress Satan’s lies; you find victory when you elevate God’s promises.

documents.excerpt: Satan loves to offer shortcuts and is really good at making them look nice, which is why the message is called “No Shortcuts.” There are no shortcuts in the Christian life and no easy way to spiritual victory: the perfect Son of God had to hang on a tree and be buried in a tomb before he could sit on a throne. If Jesus had to suffer, why would you get a shortcut?

If Jesus had to suffer, why would you get a shortcut?

Last week Pastor Steve showed that Satan loves to take a good thing like bread and make it the main thing, turning God’s gifts into gods. True believers answer, “I’d rather be starving with Jesus than stuffed without him; I’d rather be living on the street and have Jesus than be in a mansion without him.”

We reserve isolation for our worst criminals; after 40 days alone, Jesus sees all the nations, people, communities, connection, fellowship, power, and influence.
excerpts: All the kingdoms of the world: Josh assumes all means all, and the view must have been breathtaking, especially for a lonely Jesus. We reserve isolation for our worst criminals; after 40 days alone, Jesus sees all the nations, people, communities, connection, fellowship, power, and influence.

Josh remembers watching the sunrise from Haleakalā on his Hawaii honeymoon, freezing but remarkable, standing on solid ground looking down on the clouds. Still, it’s hard to imagine the magnitude of the supernatural display Jesus encountered.

The closest modern comparison is Central Park Tower in New York City, the tallest residential building in the world, with a penthouse listed at $250 million. Imagine waking up to that view every morning, and even more, the pride that could build up in someone with the posture of being above it all.

excerpts: The message of a suffering servant wasn’t new; it had been on the lips of God’s prophets for thousands of years, beginning with Moses. On the road to Emmaus, Jesus got frustrated with two men who saw the glory of the kingdom but didn’t understand the suffering: “How foolish you are… Did not the Messiah have to suffer these things and then enter his glory?”

The Scriptures foretell the suffering. Josh puts a list on the screen as homework: Genesis 3, Deuteronomy 18, Numbers 21, Isaiah 53, Daniel 9, Isaiah 9, the Psalms (“probably 110, 116, don’t quote me on that”), and Malachi 4. God has been working on this plan throughout history, and the second temptation is the prince of this world’s attempt to tear it all down: “Jesus, there doesn’t need to be suffering. We can end suffering today, right here, right now.”

Is this your attitude toward stuff? Do you consider it garbage? That word is a nasty one; Paul used a four-letter word, “dung,” and Josh won’t use the modern equivalents. Your dream home, career, health, influence: so many of us are pursuing garbage. Stop filling your life with junk and calling it blessing.

excerpts: Some say Adam gave the world over to the devil. In Genesis 1 God said, “Let us make human beings in our image, in our likeness, so that they may rule.” That authority was given to Adam; he was passive, which led to disobedience, and he handed it over to the devil.

excerpts: The other view is that this is the ultimate bluff. Satan is a liar, pretending to offer Jesus something that isn’t his to offer, and even if he had it, he wouldn’t keep his word.

Bottom line, Satan knows Jesus’ earthly ministry will exalt Yahweh, reconcile the people to God forever, and lead the nations to worship God only, which is why he says, “If you worship me, it will all be yours.” This is not a new play: Satan does in the desert what Isaiah says he did in heaven. He wanted to be worshiped, and if he could get the Son of God to worship him, “I will be like the Most High.”
Satan failed. Jesus was hungry, but he had everything he needed.

documents.context: Josh Wyatt · November 17, 2024 · Temptation: The Temptations of Jesus
documents.excerpt: Many Christians seem to have mastered the intellectual exercise of Christianity but struggle with the identity part. You can memorize Scripture, toss it out in life group, and have your theology organized, but do you believe it?
excerpts: Many Christians seem to have mastered the intellectual exercise of Christianity but struggle with the identity part. You can memorize Scripture, toss it out in life group, and have your theology organized, but do you believe it?

Satan says to Jesus, “If you are the Son of God.” Satan knows he is, Jesus knows he is, everyone there knows, but it doesn’t matter what you know: if Satan can stir up even a little doubt, he will, and he will use everything you know against you. If you’re a child of God, how come you lost your job, your home? How come your marriage is so toxic? Doesn’t he love you?

That’s Satan’s game. If you’re doing well, God must approve of you, and in the goodness Satan builds your pride. If you’re doing poorly, God must not approve, so you try to change your behavior. But behavior change comes from your abilities; heart change comes from the Lord. You need a new heart.

Proverbs 10 says the blessing of the Lord makes rich and adds no sorrow with it. God’s blessings come with joy, not sorrow, so if you claim to be surrounded by blessings and feel miserable all the time, you might need to double-check the source. God’s blessings don’t bear bad fruit.

documents.context: Josh Wyatt · November 17, 2024 · Temptation: The Temptations of Jesus
documents.excerpt: Jesus is fasting, filled with the Spirit, and in complete submission to God’s will, and he answers, “It is written: Worship the Lord your God and serve him only.”
excerpts: Jesus is fasting, filled with the Spirit, and in complete submission to God’s will, and he answers, “It is written: Worship the Lord your God and serve him only.”

A tragedy in the American church is that worship and service have become separate: many worship, few serve; many sing, few offer their gifts in service of others. But whatever we worship we will serve. Satan wasn’t asking Jesus to sing him a Chris Tomlin song; “worship me” meant “serve me”: make me the object of your greatest affection, the thing you give your time, heart, and money to, the thing you obey and teach your kids to obey.

documents.context: Josh Wyatt · November 17, 2024 · Temptation: The Temptations of Jesus
documents.excerpt: Josh’s favorite moment of worship in Scripture is Daniel in the lions’ den. Like Jesus, Daniel refused to compromise the worship of God even facing death: King Darius forbade praying to anyone but him, Daniel kept praying to Yahweh, and God shut the lions’ mouths.
excerpts: Josh’s favorite moment of worship in Scripture is Daniel in the lions’ den. Like Jesus, Daniel refused to compromise the worship of God even facing death: King Darius forbade praying to anyone but him, Daniel kept praying to Yahweh, and God shut the lions’ mouths.

Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego refused to bow to Nebuchadnezzar’s golden image and were thrown into the furnace, but there was a fourth man in the fire, a protector and savior. Josh believes Jesus was with them; the crowd didn’t see the fourth man until the door closed, but those young men of faith saw him every day.

Moses destroyed the golden calf and led Israel to repent. Elijah confronted Ahab and the prophets of Baal on Mount Carmel, “talk about a showdown,” and God answered with fire from heaven. Noah kept building, Mordecai refused to bow, Nehemiah kept working on the wall, Peter kept preaching, and Paul kept traveling.

Josh’s favorite is Joshua, who, surrounded by nations serving other gods, made his allegiance clear: if serving the Lord seems undesirable to you, choose for yourselves whom you will serve, “but as for me and my household, we will serve the Lord.” Nothing about serving the Lord seems undesirable to Josh. He has made his choice; whether God tears down or builds up, he will praise him, and no matter how attractive the world pretends to be, he will worship almighty God and serve him only.

documents.excerpt: Josh doesn’t want to spoil it, but Jesus would walk out of the wilderness victorious. Satan didn’t give up, stop, or rest; he kept looking for opportunities to keep Jesus from God’s will, and he didn’t always use prideful dictators: sometimes he dressed up like a dear friend.
excerpts: Josh doesn’t want to spoil it, but Jesus would walk out of the wilderness victorious. Satan didn’t give up, stop, or rest; he kept looking for opportunities to keep Jesus from God’s will, and he didn’t always use prideful dictators: sometimes he dressed up like a dear friend.
Stay frosty, watchful, on your toes. The winner of this showdown has been decided, but Satan still prowls around like a lion looking for someone to devour, so we cannot let our guard down.

When Satan starts talking and you recognize it, you have Josh’s permission to talk back with all the power of the Spirit of God in you: “Get back, Satan, you have no power over me, because the one who is in me is greater than you.” Whatever power Satan has, we have more. We are co-heirs with Christ, and if God is for us, who can be against us? Josh is an adopted child of almighty God; he might suffer, but one day the Lord will pry open the heavens, every knee will bow, and every tongue will confess that Jesus Christ is Lord.

documents.excerpt: One of Steve’s all-time favorite Bible heroes is John the Baptist, who was “kind of a freak”: a child of the desert with dark leathery skin, a leather wardrobe, and a diet of locusts and wild honey. excerpts: One of Steve’s all-time favorite Bible heroes is John the Baptist, who was “kind of a freak”: a child of the desert with dark leathery skin, a leather wardrobe, and a diet of locusts and wild honey. RFK Jr. would have gone ballistic: bugs and sweets. No wonder the elite said he was unstable.

He stomped around the desert with untamed dreads and bugs in his teeth, always yelling “Repent!” The authorities couldn’t stop him because he was sent from God as his chosen voice calling in the wilderness: prepare the way for the Lord.
Preaching his one-word sermon by the Jordan, “Repent, for the kingdom of heaven is at hand,” not even John knew how at hand it was.

documents.excerpt: John looks up and here comes Jesus to be baptized. When Jesus came up out of the water, heaven opened, the Spirit of God descended like a dove, and the Father said, “This is my Son, whom I love; with him I am well pleased.”
excerpts: John looks up and here comes Jesus to be baptized. When Jesus came up out of the water, heaven opened, the Spirit of God descended like a dove, and the Father said, “This is my Son, whom I love; with him I am well pleased.”

Steve offers what he calls a far better translation: “in whom my pleasure rests.” It speaks of the Father’s permanent, lasting pleasure, not the fleeting pride we feel when our kids perform, but an abiding pleasure, like drinking in the love while your baby naps.

excerpts: When Josh was about ten, they played burnout, and Josh fired one so hard Steve’s mitt cracked and his hand stung. Steve looked at his son with resting pleasure, remembering further back to the Velcro glove and Josh’s first real glove. At first Josh couldn’t catch a cold; he burst into tears, hid the mitt in the closet, and didn’t touch it for weeks.

Then one evening Steve showed him how to hold it and gently tossed the ball into his open mitt. Josh closed his hand, the glove did the rest, and Steve shouted, “Great catch, Josh!” The next night Josh said, “You throw me the ball and then say ‘great catch.’”

excerpts: Before getting to what Satan said, Steve explains how temptation happens, because Satan tempts us essentially the way he tempted Jesus. He always plays dirty, but he always fights predictably; he isn’t very creative and doesn’t have to be.

In the first century the apostle John revealed Satan’s playbook, and not one word has changed: do not love the world; everything in the world, the cravings of sinful man, the lust of his eyes, and the boasting of what he has and does, comes not from the Father but from the world.

Every day our minds are bombarded with sights and sounds designed to feed these three appetites, and every human has all three in spades. Temptations aimed at them produce desires, feelings, and longings that make us want to act, and that is where the battle is always fought.

documents.excerpt: As a young man Steve was struggling with temptation and losing battle after battle. excerpts: The church opens its doors to everyone, because the gospel must be preached to all. But while everyone hears it, responses and obedience will vary. Josh points to the parable of the sower in Matthew 13 and urges people to memorize its principles: the seed of truth, that Jesus came to save sinners and will purify you if you repent, is scattered. Some do nothing with it, some a little, and a very small group experience complete life change.

What is often forgotten is that someone who does nothing with it doesn’t necessarily stop attending church. The overflow of faithful believers is so great it benefits even people who want nothing to do with Jesus as Lord.

Many Christians have a childlike optimism that everyone is living what they learn; relationships in the church quickly force you out of it. The church isn’t only good soil; some people are hard as a path, rocky, or thorny. Don’t assume everyone here is surrendered to Jesus, or always obedient even if they are.
You don’t need an emotional flak jacket for the next relational grenade, but this family is a messy place, with people in all different places in their walk with Christ.

excerpts: We are led not only by the word but by obedient men and women who lead by example. Josh reads verses 7 through 9: Paul worked night and day so as not to be a burden, to offer himself as a model to imitate.

Effective Christian influence comes when you can point to your life as an example of obedience. It is the difference between title and tenure. Josh’s legal title is “governing authority,” which makes him laugh, since without Jesus he couldn’t govern his own life; Jesus is the governing authority. Anyone can have a title, but tenure is earned. For over a decade he has confessed his darkest moments and how Jesus rescued and restored him, and the church accepted him. He doesn’t care about his title; he cares whether he lives in a way worthy of it.

excerpts: Josh reads verses 10 through 12: anyone unwilling to work shall not eat; some among you are not busy but busybodies; settle down and earn the bread you eat.

Teaching his kids hard work is a comedy sketch. Madison used to dodge work but is now a hard worker; Nolan, 10, is a work in progress. Pulling weeds after a June monsoon, Josh wrecks the yard while Nolan walks by the same weed fourteen times, as if he needs a friendship with the weed before uprooting its life. Parenting is God’s favorite way to build humility and patience; God asks how many years Josh refused to pick up his cross.

Some people talk about Scripture in a fantastical, philosophical way with a heightened embrace of mystery unlike anything he has heard in a lifetime under godly men.
excerpts: Unplanned, Josh calls out something specific to this church. Famous pastors on YouTube preach generally; he can preach specifically. Some people talk about Scripture in a fantastical, philosophical way with a heightened embrace of mystery unlike anything he has heard in a lifetime under godly men.

Then it clicked: they want to see beyond what they are supposed to see, insisting there is more when there isn’t. Here is how you go deeper: do it. Pick up your cross and do it. A philosophy degree isn’t building disciples; it is creating confusion. If God wanted you to know it, he would have told you; one day we’ll know fully. If you discovered something 1,900 years of faithful Christians never saw, that is a red flag; it probably isn’t Christian.

documents.excerpt: Are you content in the little things? Verse 13: never tire of doing what is good. Josh wants it on a T-shirt and quotes it to himself all week; Paul told the Galatians the same thing, let us not become weary in doing good. It is his battle cry for ministry and for Crossroads Cares.
excerpts: Are you content in the little things? Verse 13: never tire of doing what is good. Josh wants it on a T-shirt and quotes it to himself all week; Paul told the Galatians the same thing, let us not become weary in doing good. It is his battle cry for ministry and for Crossroads Cares.

This is one of the most generous churches Josh has ever seen; if he didn’t think so, he’d probably be gone. But they have helped pay people’s mortgages only to see them disappear: did we just get taken for a ride? Maybe, but we can’t let those who take advantage change our readiness to care for those who truly need us.

David says the wicked borrow and do not repay, but the righteous give generously, and blessed are those who have regard for the weak. In Acts 20 Paul recalls Jesus’ words: it is more blessed to give than to receive. Our job is to make sure the brother or sister next to us isn’t growing weary of the good work.

documents.excerpt: Josh reads verses 14 and 15: take special note of those who don’t obey; don’t associate with them so they may feel ashamed, yet don’t regard them as enemies but warn them as fellow believers. Love keeps no record of wrongs, but it seems necessary to keep a record of wrongdoers.
excerpts: Josh reads verses 14 and 15: take special note of those who don’t obey; don’t associate with them so they may feel ashamed, yet don’t regard them as enemies but warn them as fellow believers. Love keeps no record of wrongs, but it seems necessary to keep a record of wrongdoers.

No one talks about church discipline anymore; it isn’t “church cool.” A soft, passive stance blows Josh’s mind, because Jesus clearly addresses it. Many think it is a spiritual SWAT team of elders pouncing on anyone in sin. Should you live in sin as a believer? No. Should we kick you out right away? No; this is precisely where you need to be until you prove you don’t want to be here.
Many have a negative view because they sat under dictators, not pastors. Think of a good parent disciplining a child: correcting love.

From pastoral counsel: if you fear for your physical safety, do not go alone; sometimes you need to establish a testimony sooner. Use discernment and seek wisdom; that isn’t gossip when you are honestly trying to honor God in a complicated situation.

Help them understand, but if they persist, rebuke them, as Paul called out Peter in Antioch.

Then sit and work it through, or find someone who can. Or do they keep ignoring believer after believer and church after church? Help them understand, but if they persist, rebuke them, as Paul called out Peter in Antioch.

If you need help deciding whether an issue matters, ask a pastor or elder. James 5: whoever turns a sinner from the way of error will save them from death and cover over a multitude of sins. Nobody comes out a winner in church discipline, but no church discipline smells way worse. Nobody wants this place to turn into a Circle K bathroom.

documents.context: Josh Wyatt · November 3, 2024 · The Invisible Enemy
documents.excerpt: Sinners aren’t the battlefield; they’re the mission field. You aren’t out to execute them but to exonerate them, and the mission field is harder work than the battlefield.
excerpts: Sinners aren’t the battlefield; they’re the mission field. You aren’t out to execute them but to exonerate them, and the mission field is harder work than the battlefield.

Sometimes the best thing you can do for an unrepentant sinner is pull your relationship. If you keep the same fellowship with disobedient Christians as with obedient ones, you put your stamp of approval on their sin; if you don’t call them out, you might as well cheer them on. Whose sin are you approving by not saying the hard truth?

Issues in the church mean issues in people’s hearts. Some know they need help, some don’t, some refuse it, but we must always offer it, always forgive, always seek to restore, and always build up the church.

documents.context: Josh Wyatt · November 3, 2024 · The Invisible Enemy
documents.excerpt: Someone asked Kristen why her cross necklace was sideways; she didn’t know. Josh told her to say that’s what a cross looks like when it’s being carried. Many are sitting and watching when they should be carrying.
excerpts: Someone asked Kristen why her cross necklace was sideways; she didn’t know. Josh told her to say that’s what a cross looks like when it’s being carried. Many are sitting and watching when they should be carrying.

For some, carrying your cross and denying yourself means forgiving the unforgivable today; for others, realizing you are the one who needs to be forgiven. Deny yourself, pick up your cross, and follow me. Jesus gave up everything; why can’t you give anything up? There is a crown on the other side. Give it up, die to self, surrender.

Josh prays over what he calls a housekeeping message, a family meeting: the work is eternal and actions have consequences. He asks the Lord to help them live like him, change and soften them, forgive them, teach them to forgive others, and make this place shine.

documents.excerpt: Continuing the series in 2 Thessalonians 2, a short chapter of 17 verses, Josh asks if anyone has ever been misquoted to their face: “This is what I heard.” Often people share something encouraging the Lord gave them from his sermon that he doesn’t think he said; usually it is funny and positive.
excerpts: Continuing the series in 2 Thessalonians 2, a short chapter of 17 verses, Josh asks if anyone has ever been misquoted to their face: “This is what I heard.” Often people share something encouraging the Lord gave them from his sermon that he doesn’t think he said; usually it is funny and positive.

Other times it causes problems: “Josh, you said this and I disagree.” YouTube lets him say “go check tape,” but every word is recorded and archived, so he must say what is true and communicate it clearly. Effective communication is hard; words can be misheard, misinterpreted, and misunderstood.

documents.excerpt: Paul faced this with the Thessalonians. He had been with them, broken bread with them, and sent one letter to comfort them by explaining the day of the Lord, yet some still misunderstood its timing. Told it could be at any moment, some quit their jobs and stopped caring for their families and communities, and intense persecution convinced others the day had come.
excerpts: Paul faced this with the Thessalonians. He had been with them, broken bread with them, and sent one letter to comfort them by explaining the day of the Lord, yet some still misunderstood its timing. Told it could be at any moment, some quit their jobs and stopped caring for their families and communities, and intense persecution convinced others the day had come.

So Paul “powered up Microsoft Word” to write another letter, because a distracted, confused church is not a healthy church. The rumors encouraged complacency, but the Lord’s day builds urgency. Paul says: hold up, several things must happen before Christ returns. In the meantime stop guessing and staring at the sky; hold fast to the gospel, pray, share the reason for the hope you have as his ambassadors, and don’t be idle.

History has seen evil leaders like Nero and Domitian, Stalin and Hitler, and church history is loaded with false messiahs, cult leaders, and wolves in sheep’s clothing. But one is still to come who will make them all look elementary, the most wicked, deceitful, and powerful man ever.

Paul calls him the man of lawlessness, the man doomed to destruction, the lawless one; John calls him the Antichrist. In 1 John: “Dear children, this is the last hour… even now many antichrists have come.” Anyone who opposes the person and work of Christ operates by the spirit of the Antichrist.

In Pharaoh’s court (go watch The Prince of Egypt), Pharaoh’s yes-men copied Moses in the name of their cheap god Ra, but Moses’ staff ate theirs. God’s miracles lead people to the truth; the Antichrist’s lead people to believe his lies.

Stand firm and hold fast
This is your purpose. The world would love nothing more than for you to be a Christian without a firm grasp of God’s word. The secret power of lawlessness seeks to tear the Christian from the word while keeping them close enough to think they’re still a Christian.
It loves that you show up early, before the countdown, while week after week you delay getting in the water to declare your faith in baptism. What are you waiting for? If you won’t embrace the title “sinner saved by grace” in here, will you out there?
documents.title: Stand firm and hold fast — The Lawless One

documents.excerpt: Being here, on the prayer team, hosting a life group, tithing, singing, or attending every week doesn’t mean you love him. Judas served on Jesus’ team but didn’t love him. Examine yourself right now.
excerpts: Being here, on the prayer team, hosting a life group, tithing, singing, or attending every week doesn’t mean you love him. Judas served on Jesus’ team but didn’t love him. Examine yourself right now.

Jesus says if you love me you’ll obey me. You’re so close; how can you do nothing with what you’ve heard? He says repent. He says let your light shine; why is yours under a bowl? He says cut it off if it causes you to stumble, and you sweep it under the rug. He says be perfect, and he means it. He says seek God’s kingdom first, and all you seek is your career. He says don’t worry about tomorrow, forgive, lead by serving, love him with all your heart, mind, and soul, love your neighbor, teach others to obey him, deny yourself, give to those who can’t repay. Do this because you love me.

None of your actions matter if you don’t love him or haven’t been filled with the Holy Spirit. What will Jesus say face to face: “She’s with me. He’s with me,” or “I never knew you; away from me, you worker of iniquity”? Examine yourselves to see whether you are in the faith. God is patient but won’t hold back forever. Repent, be baptized, go and sin no more.

documents.excerpt: Josh invites the church backstage: he plans a year of teaching at a time and prays over it for weeks, yet is willing to abandon the plan when something needs to be said among the family.
excerpts: Josh invites the church backstage: he plans a year of teaching at a time and prays over it for weeks, yet is willing to abandon the plan when something needs to be said among the family.

Some claim planning cuts out the Holy Spirit, a “bottle-fed diaper Christian view of the Holy Spirit.” If he is surrendered to the Spirit and walking by him, his planning will be Spirit-led too; the Spirit moves on Tuesday every bit as much as on Sunday.

Last November he placed this series here knowing it was an election year, because the cave-dwelling Christians would emerge to say the country will collapse unless you vote for their candidate. It is a message of fear from people who aren’t supposed to live in fear.

Our Lord didn’t give us a political system to change the world; he gave us the church, and promised the gates of hell will not overcome it. “Your message of fear is rebuked in this place.” If you want a political commentator, find another church; if you want a pastor who preaches Christ crucified, stay as long as you like.

documents.excerpt: Josh holds up the stack of election mail, including his wife’s ballot, which they haven’t filled out yet, and teases the plain black-and-white publicity pamphlet. “These, Christian, are not your voting guide. This is,” he says of the Bible.
excerpts: Josh holds up the stack of election mail, including his wife’s ballot, which they haven’t filled out yet, and teases the plain black-and-white publicity pamphlet. “These, Christian, are not your voting guide. This is,” he says of the Bible.

Statistics say one in four in the room plan to vote yes on Prop 139. The message that sends: God is just but his people don’t care. Shouldn’t my vote save innocent children, protect the physical and mental health of women, declare all life valuable, and give a voice to the voiceless made in God’s image? We can put a man on the moon but can’t care for women and children at the same time; we must do both. No to Prop 139: not a political issue but a biblical and moral one.

Prop 313 ensures child traffickers are put away for life; Josh will vote yes. Deuteronomy 24:7 says the kidnapper must die: purge the evil from among you, which isn’t just an Old Testament thing. How many times would someone ignore their conscience to kidnap a child?

Prop 314 would let border agents enforce immigration law. There is a right and a wrong way to enter the country. Numbers 32: the Israelites armed for battle while their women and children lived in fortified cities for protection. If their women and children deserved to feel safe, so do ours.
Bad presidents don’t last forever, but bad policies always outlast bad politicians. That is why we need good, vocal Christians. God is just; his people must act justly.

documents.excerpt: Verse 9: everlasting destruction and being shut out from the presence of the Lord. Only once did God shut out someone who was seeking him and saying “Thy will be done.” On the cross God didn’t throw stones at Jesus or toss him in the fire; he turned his back. About three in the afternoon Jesus cried out, “My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?”

Jesus was forsaken so that you could be forgiven.

excerpts: Josh reads Paul’s closing prayer, verses 11 and 12: that God would make you worthy of his calling, so that the name of our Lord Jesus may be glorified in you and you in him. Marveling at Christ isn’t only for the final day; it can start now, here, at home, in your neighborhood.

When worried, it is easy to take our eyes off Jesus and manage anxiety on our own. The key isn’t managing anxiety but marveling at Jesus all the more. If you doubt, marvel at Jesus in Gethsemane: God doesn’t need you doubt-free, just obedient. If you lack patience or forgiveness, marvel at how patient and forgiving God has been with you.

The ability to glorify Christ comes only through an experience of God’s grace. You can try really hard to be like Jesus, or marvel at Jesus and let his power transform you. WWJD is good; it is even better to ask what Jesus has done.

documents.context: Josh Wyatt · October 13, 2024 · The Invisible Enemy
documents.excerpt: Besides coming home to his wife and kids, these minutes of the body of Christ gathering to praise the Lord and receive his word are some of Josh’s favorite moments. excerpts: Besides coming home to his wife and kids, these minutes of the body of Christ gathering to praise the Lord and receive his word are some of Josh’s favorite moments. Nearly every broken home he encounters has one thing in common: worship and teaching are nowhere close to where they should be on the list of priorities.

To young parents: the odds of your child being a pro athlete are less than 1%, and skipping church for sports isn’t raising that percentage. He challenges them to compare the time a child spends on the fundamentals of their sport with the time spent on the fundamentals of their faith.

Church attendance has been declining, with a bit of a resurgence among Gen Z; recent studies show Americans attend once a month or less. We fail to saturate our children in the word of God, then shake our fist at God when our daughter goes to ASU and abandons the faith. She was a great volleyball player, but her house was built on the sand.
Worship together, pray together, be in the word together: daily in your house and weekly in his house.

These people need to be dealt with immediately, and you don’t have to wait for leadership: you have Josh’s permission to challenge it. Matthew 18: go to them; if you can’t win them over, bring someone; if that fails, bring them to the church. Otherwise they become bitter, a pariah. It is our job to make sure the unruly don’t rule.

Many churches are full of armchair critics. The Lord hates a person who stirs up dissension in the community. We must be bold, confident, and strong enough to warn them, with kindness and love, but we must call it out.

The disheartened are the risk-averse among us. They fear change, so they avoid a life group that might make them deal with things, avoid ministry outside their comfort zone, and don’t try things for fear of failing.
The courageous Christian is called to lock arms with the disheartened and walk together. Too often the courageous all end up in one spot having a bonfire while the disheartened go home early. We have to do better at encouraging our discouraged brothers and sisters.

excerpts: Verse 14: Paul doesn’t mean the physically weak, though we should care for them, but the spiritually weak, those with doubts. “Anybody struggled with doubts? Come on, liars.” Those with doubts need to be strengthened by those with confidence.

Josh calls James 5 one of the most misinterpreted texts he has heard in the church: James is talking about those weak in the faith and vulnerable to attack. Most Christians stop at “the prayer offered in faith will make them well,” but James goes on: if they have sinned they will be forgiven, so confess your sins to each other and pray for each other that you may be healed.

Our weakest moments are worked out in biblical community. The church is busy concealing sin when it should be confessing, so that others can encourage us to repent. When repentance happens in community, you have an army of confident believers seeking to restore you. Josh might be strong today and weak tomorrow; we need each other, and the modern church seems to lack the humility to live this way.

excerpts: Paul knows how hard life-on-life ministry is, so he reminds us to be patient. Josh, the youngest of three after Andrea and Jessica, spent Saturday nights locked in the church office with no kids’ programming. The office ladies kept a loaded candy supply on the honor system, and Josh had no honor.

The kids wrote IOUs on sticky notes and ate all the candy. His dad was furious, paid the bill, and spanked them; they deserved it. Having seen church budgets, Josh suspects the office supply line was out of control because of their paper-clip statues and staple-gun fights.

Two of those kids are serving the church today. To children’s and youth workers: be patient. That kid hitting his head against the wall might end up a pastor, and you might end up in one of his sermons.

excerpts: Josh admits he can get fiery and understands wanting payback, especially against a believer who should know better. But the clear instruction is not to repay evil for evil; the Christian waits patiently and trusts the Lord to sort it out.

The Christian living in sin wants him to stop preaching there: “Let me do my thing; I need some privacy.” But doing good for someone doing wrong isn’t pretending it didn’t happen. You don’t look out for someone’s good by ignoring their wrong.

Healthy, mature Christians walk that tightrope imperfectly, willing to have uncomfortable conversations in love and patience without choking the truth. If someone won’t tell you what you need to hear for fear of hurting your feelings, they aren’t striving for your good; they’re making way for you to keep doing wrong.

excerpts: Some of Josh’s most memorable worship came on the heels of his most painful moments. The first time he worshiped here after his sister passed away was one of the most intimate times of worship he has had. He doesn’t remember the songs or who was there; it was just him and God. He was hurting, and God was helping.

He would hardly call that time joyful, yet he was rejoicing: his pain colliding with his confidence. His body shook, but his faith didn’t quiver once. He can’t stay down long because God has loved him, saved him, provided for him, and promises more. Paul’s words encourage him: our present sufferings are not worth comparing with the glory that will be revealed in us.

Josh tells them what to pray, Isaiah 41:10: do not fear, for I am with you; I will strengthen you and help you; I will uphold you with my righteous right hand. He models it: “Lord, I pray for Luke that he would not live in fear but remember that you’re with him forever.”

The hard part: while here, find someone to pray for out loud. Four weeks left means four people here and 28 at home. If you don’t know 28 people, introduce yourself at the water station and ask their name. Don’t take the bracelet if you won’t lean in. The enemy isn’t taking long weekends, and neither should we.

documents.context: Steve Wyatt · October 6, 2024 · The Invisible Enemy
documents.excerpt: That longing is how Jesus wants it: not yearning to the point of distraction, as if his return were the only thing we think about, but not yawning to the point of indifference either. Jesus clearly said he is coming soon, and the Bible gives clear signs meant to suggest it really is almost time. And it is, because it is always almost time.
excerpts: That longing is how Jesus wants it: not yearning to the point of distraction, as if his return were the only thing we think about, but not yawning to the point of indifference either. Jesus clearly said he is coming soon, and the Bible gives clear signs meant to suggest it really is almost time. And it is, because it is always almost time.

Jesus wants us always looking for signs that his return is nearer than ever, and he said they would increase exponentially as a signal to anyone who lifts up their head that our redemption is drawing near. What fascinates Steve about our time is that more of these signs are happening in closer proximity than ever before.

If they really are signs, his return could happen, as Paul said, in the twinkling of an eye. Maybe the voice of the archangel and the trumpet of God are warming up even now. A twinkling, Steve says, is less than a full twink; call it half a twink, not enough time for one decent blink, and we could be in the presence of Jesus.

documents.context: Steve Wyatt · October 6, 2024 · The Invisible Enemy
documents.excerpt: So let’s talk about it, not to the point of distraction, but for the reason Jesus gave the signs: so we would be ready, because even with increasing signs he will come at a time we don’t expect.
excerpts: So let’s talk about it, not to the point of distraction, but for the reason Jesus gave the signs: so we would be ready, because even with increasing signs he will come at a time we don’t expect.

End-times talk isn’t an academic itch for Steve. He doesn’t care about identifying key players or plotting dates, and he has little patience with dogmatic theorists who parse prophecy like a theological gnat-swallowing contest. That bores him; Jesus’ soon return doesn’t bore him at all, “that puppy flips all my switches.” What bores him is people strumming the same tune on a one-string guitar about their chosen position. Give it up.

He will unpack a few interpretations, but don’t race up to him in the lobby expecting him to spend three minutes convincing you his is right. As long as we agree Jesus is coming in a physical, visible return, and soon, we’re good. Most of the rest is above his pay grade, and yours too.

People wrestle with that: it has been 2,000 years, and by any human standard that isn’t soon. Steve agrees, but Jesus isn’t human. Steve believes the seven-year tribulation comes after Jesus takes his church. Imagine one or two billion God-fearing, taxpaying, government-respecting, morally upright believers suddenly gone; that will trigger chaos. Into it steps the Antichrist, whose first big act is a peace treaty with Israel. Halfway through he breaks it, and a greater tribulation lasts another three and a half years. It is prophesied in Daniel and described in greater detail in Revelation. There is no small disagreement about how these events unfold, but vast agreement that these are the events, and Steve really doesn’t think believers will be here for it.

excerpts: Until then, if you feel restless in your relationships, your family, or maintaining your purity, priorities, and commitments, God wants you to feel that, because you are not yet with him, and he made you to be with him. Your heart won’t find its rest, and that longing won’t be satisfied, until you see Jesus face to face. He made you for pleasures this world can’t provide and a glory you can’t imagine: no eye has seen, no ear has heard.

That day is coming. You will see Jesus face to face and join the redeemed from every tribe and nation, singing and shouting praise to the God who made you and saved you. You will know what your mind couldn’t contain, see beauty and colors you never knew existed, hear music you could never conceive, walk on streets of gold, and meet Peter, James, and John. He reads it: seed on the path eaten by birds, seed on rocky places that sprang up and withered for lack of root, seed among thorns that choked it, and seed on good soil that produced a crop thirty, sixty, a hundred times. He reads it: seed on the path eaten by birds, seed on rocky places that sprang up and withered for lack of root, seed among thorns that choked it, and seed on good soil that produced a crop thirty, sixty, a hundred times. It is timeless: there are still four kinds of hearts that respond to God’s message four ways.

excerpts: Josh hopes this six-week series through First and 2 Thessalonians builds the church’s faith and strengthens believers, which is why Paul wrote. It was one of his first letters, around AD 51, to a church established only two or three months earlier, and he builds their faith by correcting misconceptions about the resurrection of the dead and the second coming of Christ.

The series skips much of the first half, where Paul is being their pastor: thanking God for their faith and for their reputation in the city, which matters to God and should matter to us. He has been in their living rooms, sent Timothy, misses them, and longs to be with them. He prays things like “May the Lord increase your love,” the kind of prayer we should pray over each other, so they can be blameless before God when Jesus comes. We like Paul the apostle, but this is Paul the pastor, and he loved and served his people well.

That is why the porn industry is straight from the devil himself, and going by the numbers, some invite the devil into their home weekly. It has trained urges and desires toward a prerecorded stranger when those God-given impulses are meant to drive you to the marriage bed. Hebrews 13 says marriage should be honored by all and the marriage bed kept pure, for God will judge the adulterer and all the sexually immoral.
Godly sexuality is real, satisfying, and good; Satan’s counterfeit is empty and destructive. The world always offers alternatives. Josh’s one piece of advice: flee the offers of counterfeit intimacy. Young ladies especially: no intimacy is better than counterfeit intimacy. Flee.
documents.title: God’s user manual — Are You Ready?

The context: young Christians were quitting their jobs to wait for Christ’s return. They weren’t working, and believers and unbelievers alike were impacted by freeloaders. Paul says no: our reputation matters. Don’t stir up trouble; live together and contribute to your communities; stop being idle.

documents.excerpt: In some places Paul seems to hope he will be alive when Jesus returns. Who could blame him? Who here wants to be alive when Jesus returns? At other times he thinks he may die first, as in 1 Corinthians 6: by his power God raised the Lord from the dead, and he will raise us also.
excerpts: In some places Paul seems to hope he will be alive when Jesus returns. Who could blame him? Who here wants to be alive when Jesus returns? At other times he thinks he may die first, as in 1 Corinthians 6: by his power God raised the Lord from the dead, and he will raise us also.

It’s okay to desire to be among the living, as long as you aren’t devastated to be among the dead. It’s okay to wrestle with this, but we need more Christians who will end the race well. Paul wrestled in Philippians 1: Christ will be exalted in my body, whether by life or by death; for to me, to live is Christ and to die is gain.
For everyone in Christ, both remain possible: we will either rise or be caught up. Either way we have nothing to fear, because Jesus is coming with us or for us. Maranatha. Come, Lord Jesus.

documents.excerpt: Luke dedicates more than half of Acts to Paul’s ministry. Paul and Barnabas sail to Cyprus and cross the whole island on foot preaching in the synagogues, sail north to Perga, hike to Galatia, turn to the Gentiles when the Jews reject the message, and are driven out of Antioch. They just keep going.
excerpts: Luke dedicates more than half of Acts to Paul’s ministry. Paul and Barnabas sail to Cyprus and cross the whole island on foot preaching in the synagogues, sail north to Perga, hike to Galatia, turn to the Gentiles when the Jews reject the message, and are driven out of Antioch. They just keep going.

Josh was convicted this week by their tenacity. It is easy to get shut down and back into silence, and modern Christians are guilty of it; honestly, we are soft. We will say hard things in here where we get amens, but at any resistance out there we zip it up and snuggle into Christian circles where the worst thing anyone will say is “He’s a Calvinist.” We have mastered echo chambers where everything gets applause.

The culture is demanding a shift to a more Pauline ministry approach: speak where it’s hard to speak, where people don’t invite you to speak. And when you preach, don’t sweat the outcome. Some will reject it, some will accept it; that’s between them and God. Your job is to share it.

excerpts: Later Paul and Barnabas have a disagreement and part ways before the second missionary journey. This took Josh a long time to learn. He used to be devastated when someone left the church, taking weeks to get over it, whether they wrote ten-page letters about how horrible he is or simply stopped coming without saying goodbye.

When you lift up the mission of the church in prayer, we always pray for God to bring people to help. We never think to pray for the right people to leave. But the Lord knows what you need before you ask; he’ll clear it out.

Crossroads set out to build the most giving, selfless, over-the-top loving and generous church on the planet; it’s part of Josh’s daily prayers. God brought some of the most generous, loving, selfless, kind people he has ever met, and he also removed some of the least generous, most selfish, most toxic. When people leave, the finance team checks the impact as good stewardship, and about 95 percent of the time they find church folks eager to supply the church with their complaining but not their currency.

excerpts: Paul’s third journey revisits many places, with an extended stay in Ephesus, and travels the southwest coast of Asia Minor. Despite the risk, he sails back to Jerusalem, gets mixed reviews, and is eventually arrested and put on trial.

It’s easy to read the last 15 chapters of Acts and forget that God used many people to spread the gospel and launch his church. Paul is a warrior for Christ, but he’d be the first to tell you about the unnamed heroes, his disciples and their disciples. The church is built on unnamed Christian heroes: the lame beggar in chapter 3 whom God used so Peter could preach to thousands; Stephen and Philip, who got things done so the apostles could preach; Cornelius, who showed Peter the gospel is for all people; James at the Jerusalem Council; women like Priscilla and Lydia. There was work for everyone.

Are you okay being an unnamed Christian?
We all have different roles. Without Chris as executive pastor, Josh wouldn’t get the better part of two days to pray over and prepare a message. Without Steve, Hunter, and Holly shepherding the church’s sons and daughters, he wouldn’t have time to sit with moms and dads working through marriages. Andrea’s and Elijah’s jobs are too big without volunteers serving communion, pointing cameras, running slides, and welcoming people. If your job is making bagels, praise God: we are partners in the gospel, and your hospitality makes guests feel at home. God can use one small act to accomplish big things.
This hits Josh too. It is important to be content to serve where God has us. This is the church God tasked him with shepherding, and he is responsible for their souls. He isn’t building a platform or a brand; he’ll let God determine his influence. Are you content being a page-eight Christian, or would you prefer the headlines?

excerpts: Paul faces trial on charges that aren’t credible. Sound familiar? Remember Pontius Pilate. Paul’s defense: if the Jews’ claims about him are false, no one has the right to hand him over to them, and he appeals to Caesar. If you wonder how Christianity went from Jerusalem to Rome, it starts in this moment in chapter 25. King Agrippa goes on record telling Festus that this man could have been set free if he had not appealed to Caesar.

Of all Paul’s journeys Rome was the most important, but it wasn’t a mission journey. No charting the route, gathering supplies, or raising funds. Paul had been in custody close to two years when Festus took over from Felix, and the second Festus reached his case, Paul appealed. It was a legal journey. Paul surely didn’t think this was how he’d get to Rome, but the Lord gave him an opportunity and he took it.

Appealing to Caesar was a first-century habeas corpus, everyone getting a day in court, except your fate is in Caesar’s hands, and Caesar was Nero, a ticking time bomb who might lop off your head to burn off frustration. Paul figures he’s already in Roman custody, so he might as well be in custody in Rome before Caesar. It’s Holy Spirit bold, “to live is Christ, to die is gain” bold.

documents.excerpt: Roman officials put Paul and 275 others on a boat to Rome; a hurricane leaves them lost at sea for nearly a month. One thing after another, yet Paul never doubts God’s sovereignty; he finds opportunity and stays an optimist no matter what.
excerpts: Roman officials put Paul and 275 others on a boat to Rome; a hurricane leaves them lost at sea for nearly a month. One thing after another, yet Paul never doubts God’s sovereignty; he finds opportunity and stays an optimist no matter what.

Satan peddles a lie among Christians that God should protect Christians from the storm. It sounds right because God is our protector, but didn’t Jesus rebuke the disciples for waking him during the storm: “Do you still have no faith?” God allows storms so people can see what faith looks like in a storm.

The world needs to see the difference between suffering and suffering with eternal hope: a cancer patient and a cancer patient with eternal hope, a grieving parent at a child’s grave and a grieving parent with eternal hope. That’s how you make the world scratch its head: in the storm you say, “Praise the Lord, my soul,” and refuse to forget all his benefits, who forgives your sins, heals your diseases, redeems your life from the pit, and renews your youth like the eagle’s.

In Romans 2 Paul says that when Gentiles who do not have the law do by nature what the law requires, they show its requirements are written on their hearts, their consciences bearing witness. excerpts: A timeless truth here: the moral law is written on the islanders’ hearts. In Romans 2 Paul says that when Gentiles who do not have the law do by nature what the law requires, they show its requirements are written on their hearts, their consciences bearing witness. Nobody taught the islanders this was good; they just knew it. God revealed himself to them, which is one reason Paul says people are without excuse: you who pass judgment on someone else condemn yourself, because you do the same things.

This answers a question many believers wrestle with: how does God deal with unreached people who haven’t heard the gospel? Josh believes God can justly condemn those who haven’t heard because they fail to keep the moral standards they impose on others. Romans 2:11: God does not show favoritism; all who sin apart from the law will perish apart from the law, and all who sin under the law will be judged by the law. What made Malta’s kindness unusual was their limited knowledge of God and his law.

So it is strange to Josh when Christians are overly concerned for unreached people groups. He isn’t saying have no concern, but the greatest concern isn’t the unreached group; it’s the reached group that turned its back on God.

God doesn’t need a lesson on justice from us. At least those tribes notice creation and the created order, acknowledge a natural and an unnatural way, and try to live the natural way. They are far better off than a nation that turned its back on God and decided it can choose its gender based on how it feels in the morning. The person who has never heard the gospel is far better off than the person who rejects it.

Josh wants the American church to drop the idea that global missions are always on some remote island. We’re losing this country. The greatest mission field is the house next door. Do we need to send a missionary to your neighbor, or can we just send you?

Get in the word, know your Savior, and speak of him to anyone who will listen.

Satan is ruthless; he won’t give you time to grab a towel. He runs at you when you’re exhausted. Stay alert, Christian. Always stay alert.

Romans 14 says we will all give an account of ourselves to God. That is scary, especially when Paul quotes Psalm 14: there is no one righteous, not even one; no one who understands, no one who seeks God; all have turned away and become worthless; no one does good, not even one. excerpts: Theologians call it the great exchange, the climax of the Christian message, the doctrine of substitution. 2 Corinthians 5:21: God made him who had no sin to be sin for us, so that in him we might become the righteousness of God.

Jesus earned righteousness; we earned God’s wrath. In an unfair trade initiated by God’s grace and mercy alone, Jesus took on God’s wrath and satisfied it completely on the cross, and we receive righteousness through him: forgiveness forever. As Peter declares, he himself bore our sins in his body on the cross, so that we might die to sins and live for righteousness; by his wounds you have been healed.

excerpts: As the ushers pass the communion elements, Josh wants to be pastoral. He senses a spirit of fear in the body of Christ. A new series, The Invisible Enemy, is about to begin, and he is disturbed and discouraged by what he sees in Christian circles as elections come around. He rebukes that spirit of fear 100 percent.

As a Christian, it is your civic duty to vote: register and go vote. Inspect who you vote for, why, and what they stand for, and vote righteousness as best you can, though that is hard to discern. Above all, pray: get on your knees for your country, your nation, voters, and your neighbor, and plead with God to soften your heart.

There’s nothing to be afraid of. The future is written: Christ reigns, and no matter who has authority until then, he comes and takes it all. He is King, Lord, and Savior. Go into these months with confidence and faith in the one who did it and is coming to wrap it all up. He loves them too much to let them live in fear: stop, look up, and remember who you serve.

documents.excerpt: There is a lot of talk about revival in the church. When revival is real, and not a hyper-emotional stage show with Benny Hinn swinging his Armani coat around slaying people in the Spirit, it is a beautiful thing. Elijah points to the First Great Awakening, when Jonathan Edwards and George Whitefield preached repentance and grace into an increasingly secular, rationalistic culture and re-energized the faith in the American colonies.

When revival is real, and not a hyper-emotional stage show with Benny Hinn swinging his Armani coat around slaying people in the Spirit, it is a beautiful thing. Elijah points to the First Great Awakening, when Jonathan Edwards and George Whitefield preached repentance and grace into an increasingly secular, rationalistic culture and re-energized the faith in the American colonies.

But for the most part revival has become sensationalized, measured by how much people get the touchy-feelies rather than whether people are being raised to spiritual life by the Holy Spirit. Churches plan revival services, not realizing revival is not up to man. Read Acts as a whole and you see that revival comes at a cost, and that it always falls under the providence of God, not man’s plans and desires.

Jesus warned his disciples about the hardship they would face. Pastor Steve encouraged the church last week with the verse Elijah wants to set the tone: John 16:33, “In this world you will have trouble, but take heart. I have overcome the world.”

excerpts: “Eli, aren’t we skipping a lot of chapters?” Yes: Acts has 28 chapters and the series has six weeks. It was never meant to be exhaustive, and if you rely on Sundays for all your Bible reading, you are missing the point.

The teaching and pastoral teams believe their job is to equip the church for the work of ministry. Ephesians 4:11 says Christ gave apostles, prophets, evangelists, shepherds, and teachers to equip the saints for the work of ministry, for building up the body of Christ. If you wait to be spoon-fed, you will starve. Give a man a fish and you feed him for a day; teach a man to fish and you feed him for a lifetime.

No one should feel left behind. If you struggle with what time with God looks like outside church, talk to any of the pastors; they are here through the week. They would much rather talk about being intentional with the Lord than read brother so-and-so’s latest end-times predictions, which Elijah just deletes at this point.

documents.excerpt: Acts 10: God uses visions to show Peter and Cornelius that the Levitical ceremonial law is fulfilled in Christ: “Do not call anything unclean that which God has called clean.” Christ is the perfect Passover lamb, so there is no need for ceremonial law. Theologians call this type and antitype: an event or person that points to a greater fulfillment. As God delivered Israel from literal bondage in the Exodus, Jesus delivers us from spiritual bondage; many call Jesus the greater Moses.

Acts 11: Peter explains his vision and the people rejoice, “So then, even to Gentiles God has granted repentance that leads to life,” and Saul and Barnabas preach in Antioch. Acts 12: Peter is arrested and broken out of prison by an angel, much to King Herod’s dismay, and Herod, worshiped as a god, is struck dead and eaten by worms. Yes, this is the New Testament.

Acts 13 and 14 are mostly missionary work. In Acts 15 Paul and Barnabas defend salvation by grace alone against the party of the Pharisees, and a letter goes to the Gentile churches with Judas and Silas. Paul circumcised Timothy because of the Jews in that area. Elijah clarifies: this was for ease of evangelism, not a salvation thing; Timothy didn’t need it, but it removed a barrier. As they delivered the Jerusalem decisions from town to town, the churches were strengthened in the faith and grew daily in numbers.

Paul likely had some trepidation; you couldn’t pay Elijah to go back somewhere like that. But without the gumption to return to a hostile place, Paul may never have met Timothy, who became an absolute warrior for the gospel. The providence of God is an amazing thing: he used imperfect men and messy situations to accomplish his perfect purpose, and he is in the same business today.

documents.excerpt: Paul and his companions were kept by the Holy Spirit from preaching in the province of Asia, the Spirit of Jesus would not let them enter Bithynia, and they went down to Troas, where Paul saw a vision of a man of Macedonia begging, “Come over to Macedonia and help us.”
excerpts: Paul and his companions were kept by the Holy Spirit from preaching in the province of Asia, the Spirit of Jesus would not let them enter Bithynia, and they went down to Troas, where Paul saw a vision of a man of Macedonia begging, “Come over to Macedonia and help us.”

Why would God forbid the gospel being preached? Simply timing. There was nothing wrong with Paul’s desire; God had another, better plan. excerpts: From 13 to 18 Elijah played guitar three to six hours a day until his fingers hurt, not to be a rock star but to get into Berklee College of Music, one of the most prestigious music schools in the world, with about a 30 percent acceptance rate at the time. He did the work, the practice, the grades, the gigging, the audition prep, and he got in.

Soon after, it became clear he was pursuing that life to run from what God was so clearly calling him into. He wishes he could say he piously laid down his will, but that would be a big fat lie: he knew God was calling him into ministry and wanted zero part of it. Church people made him queasy. “Sometimes y’all still do.” He is kidding, mostly.

Was it hard to lay down a dream he worked for tirelessly? Absolutely. Did God honor his decision to submit? 100 percent. Had he gone to Boston for four years he wouldn’t be here, and might not have the life he has: work he considers a privilege, a wife wildly out of his league he looks forward to coming home to, a beautiful home, two crazy dogs, and a bearded dragon.

Dropping out of college for ministry wasn’t his plan, but he wouldn’t do it differently, because seeing God’s faithfulness through his stupidity, rebellion, and running strengthens his faith to this day. God’s plan is always better than his: “Trust in the Lord with all your heart and lean not on your own understanding; in all your ways submit to him, and he will make your paths straight.”

documents.excerpt: Elijah thinks strong leadership is incredibly lacking in the American evangelical church. In Crossroads Cares meetings on Mondays he hears about struggling single mothers who gave up reaching out to their megachurch leadership because it was too busy planting another satellite campus or releasing its next worship album. All that influence and money, and a person in need can’t wake the sleeping giant, so they come to the little church of 400 to see if it will listen.
excerpts: Elijah thinks strong leadership is incredibly lacking in the American evangelical church. In Crossroads Cares meetings on Mondays he hears about struggling single mothers who gave up reaching out to their megachurch leadership because it was too busy planting another satellite campus or releasing its next worship album. All that influence and money, and a person in need can’t wake the sleeping giant, so they come to the little church of 400 to see if it will listen.

Crossroads is always happy to help whoever God sends, but it breaks his heart. If a church’s mission doesn’t involve consistently being the hands and feet of Jesus, it doesn’t matter how many campuses it plants, albums it releases, or conferences it hosts: it is failing. If every church cared for the people God entrusted to it instead of creating a country club atmosphere, things would look different.

The church doesn’t need more generic, repetitive CCM K-LOVE music. It needs men and women on fire for Christ, willing to go where the Lord calls and radically love those living on the margins. Rant over.

documents.excerpt: If you can put a stone in someone’s shoe to get them thinking about the gospel, you have done great work. Elijah reads Greg Koukl of Stand to Reason: there is pressure to close the sale fast, but a wise ambassador seasons his words. Sometimes the fruit is ripe and falls into your basket; usually it isn’t, and dropping a message that seems meaningless or unbelievable can make someone harder to reach. Koukl’s modest goal is to put a stone in his shoe, a nugget of truth that annoys him in a good way and keeps poking at him.

Koukl’s modest goal is to put a stone in his shoe, a nugget of truth that annoys him in a good way and keeps poking at him.

Everyone wants to be a harvester, but the church needs more gardeners: people less concerned with the harvest and more with planting, watering, and weeding until the fruit is ripe. Elijah is convinced it is a patience issue. Before talking with someone, ask, “Lord, give me one thing I can say, one question I can ask, one thought I can leave that will get them to think about the grace and mercy of the cross.” You have no idea how God will use that stone in their shoe.

The God of the universe took on flesh and gave up his life so we could know him, and we can’t lift up a song of praise for 20 minutes out of a 75-minute service? There is time set aside for fellowship. Let’s be a church that fills the room with the singing of the saints, unashamed and rowdy in our praise, treating that time like the life source it is.

Maybe that’s on him for not making it clear that worship is a priority; he is making it clear now. Just as it is important to be fed by the word, it is important to lift a song of praise with fellow believers, even in a smaller group. Paul and Silas understood this, singing with joy in the darkest of circumstances.

Maybe that’s on him for not making it clear that worship is a priority; he is making it clear now. Just as it is important to be fed by the word, it is important to lift a song of praise with fellow believers, even in a smaller group. Paul and Silas understood this, singing with joy in the darkest of circumstances.
documents.title: Being real about corporate worship — The Cost of Revival

Almost 20 years ago, newly married, he set out to prove to his new bride that he was the man of the garage by changing the oil in their Isuzu Rodeo. He pulled the bolt and watched fluid the color and consistency of cough syrup stream out: he had drained the entire transmission.

In Acts 5 the apostles are arrested and an angel rescues them overnight, and the council is perplexed: how do we stop them? documents.context: Steve Coots · September 8, 2024 · Unstoppable

So the enemy switches playbooks to an inside play: stir up strife and mistrust from within. In an oversimplification, the Hebraic Jews were the native population of Israel and the Hellenists had adopted more Greek practices, but both were true Jewish converts who believed Jesus is Messiah. This isn’t a Jew-versus-Gentile issue, which comes later in Acts; it is a squabble between brothers and sisters in Christ.
