To the second: the transfer of souls from the kingdom of darkness to the kingdom of light belongs to Jesus only. At the summer high school camp at Biola University, a structure over the parking garage reminds them that Jesus saves. If Jesus saves, the pressure is off. The success of sharing Jesus isn’t reliant on the outcome; the success is simply sharing Jesus.

Scripture also promises that when we are faithful to start such conversations, we don’t have to worry about carrying them on. Jesus told his disciples in Luke 12 not to worry how they would defend themselves before synagogues, rulers, and authorities, for the Holy Spirit will teach you at that time what you should say. Stephen is seeing that verse play out live: saturated with Scripture and ready to be an instrument of God’s power, an unstoppable combination.

excerpts: Stephen was simply restating the words of Jesus, and the chief priests had played the same lines at Jesus’ trial: “We heard him say, I will destroy this temple made with human hands, and in three days will build another not made with hands.” Jesus did say that, but he spoke of his own body, destroyed by them and raised three days later by God.

Stephen was also apparently elevating Jesus above Moses, more déjà vu. John wrote, “For the law was given through Moses; grace and truth came through Jesus Christ.” Jesus was more direct with the religious leaders in front of him: “Do not think I will accuse you before the Father. Your accuser is Moses, on whom your hopes are set.” Ouch. To people living by the law, any disruption of works-based righteousness was a real threat.

excerpts: The Sanhedrin saw that Stephen’s face was like the face of an angel. Not the chubby cherub of a 90s Christian bookstore: Luke means Stephen was completely calm, his face pure and bright, reflecting the presence of God.

When we are falsely accused, are we cool, calm, radiant, and reliant? David said in Psalm 34:5, “Those who look to him are radiant, and their faces shall never be ashamed.” God’s people, whose future is secure and whose hope is undiminished by circumstances, should be nothing short of radiant. The bigger question: are you looking to Jesus? In the middle of this mess, Stephen no doubt was.

excerpts: Verses 2 through 50 are homework: a masterful, detailed defense of the Christian faith drawing a line from the Old Testament to the rejection of Jesus, calling out the very men who rejected him to the point of death.

Stephen finishes: “You stiff-necked people… you always resist the Holy Spirit… now you have betrayed and murdered him.” Stephen had clearly never read How to Win Friends and Influence People. He calls them out for resisting the Spirit and rejecting the true purpose of the law they claimed to follow.

Paraphrasing pastor and commentator David Guzik: Stephen wasn’t interested in hearing “not guilty” from men; he wanted to hear “well done” from God his Father. He had to know by their growing agitation that things would not end well.

documents.excerpt: They covered their ears, rushed at him, dragged him out of the city, and stoned him, laying their coats at the feet of a young man named Saul. Stephen prayed, “Lord Jesus, receive my spirit,” and “Lord, do not hold this sin against them,” and he fell asleep.
excerpts: They covered their ears, rushed at him, dragged him out of the city, and stoned him, laying their coats at the feet of a young man named Saul. Stephen prayed, “Lord Jesus, receive my spirit,” and “Lord, do not hold this sin against them,” and he fell asleep.

Stoning was the law’s punishment for blasphemy, but it was no peaceful death, and this was no organized execution of deserved justice; it became mob violence against an innocent man who had spoken in the name of God. Some people go from cupping their ears to hear the truth to plugging them when it brushes against their pride.

Stephen prays for his attackers and falls asleep, a euphemism for the death of a believer, because death is not final: “Death, where is your victory? Death, where is your sting?” To be absent from the body is to be present with the Lord.

Data shows one in seven Christians worldwide face high levels of persecution, up from one in eight three years ago, a big difference across millions: hostility, restrictions, intimidation, discrimination, harassment, torture, arrest, children taken, imprisonment, and death. On U.S. soil we worry someone might think we are weird or awkward.
excerpts: Believers around the globe know real persecution. Data shows one in seven Christians worldwide face high levels of persecution, up from one in eight three years ago, a big difference across millions: hostility, restrictions, intimidation, discrimination, harassment, torture, arrest, children taken, imprisonment, and death. On U.S. soil we worry someone might think we are weird or awkward.

Persecution is to be expected; it is evidence of authentic faith, because the gospel will always be opposed and tested. Leaving the upper room on his final night, Jesus said in John 15, “If the world hates you, keep in mind that it hated me first… If they persecuted me, they will persecute you also.”

If you face no opposition for your faith, something may be off. Steve isn’t telling you to sell your house and move to North Korea, but you may need to step outside your comfort zone and start bold conversations with lost people in your life.

excerpts: So how about you? Steve prays that from this look at the first Christian martyr the church is encouraged not to run from persecution but to embrace it, as weird as that sounds, because it is a sign you are walking hand in hand with the Spirit.

In Philippians 3 Paul, the same Saul who kept watch over the coats while men stoned Stephen, writes that he counts everything as loss because of the surpassing worth of knowing Christ Jesus, that he may know him and the power of his resurrection. Yes, Lord. But wait, there’s more, and it’s not as much fun: “and may share his sufferings, becoming like him in his death.”

Truly following Christ and sharing his victory requires sharing his suffering, and Christians across the world embrace it. Are we prepared to stand firm in Christ if and when it comes to our doorstep?

As their pastor he has a front-row seat as believers fix their eyes on Jesus and embrace the Spirit’s ministry, through trouble or triumph.

Addicts are turning from addiction, finding healing in Jesus’ name, and moving from idols into kingdom work. Almost weekly, men tell him they are no longer content with the world’s mold of a father; some who knowingly were bad fathers a year ago now see their duty as provider, protector, and priest in the home, leading their wives and children in the ways of the Lord. documents.context: Josh Wyatt · September 1, 2024 · Unstoppable
documents.excerpt: Extraordinary things are happening in Jerusalem after Pentecost; Jesus is showing off through the apostles. Josh won’t tell anyone these things don’t happen anymore. People try to label him with man-made doctrines, but he dodges the labels; he isn’t a cessationist. God works how he wants, when he wants, period.
excerpts: Extraordinary things are happening in Jerusalem after Pentecost; Jesus is showing off through the apostles. Josh won’t tell anyone these things don’t happen anymore. People try to label him with man-made doctrines, but he dodges the labels; he isn’t a cessationist. God works how he wants, when he wants, period.

When amazing things happen, he isn’t amazed at the things themselves or the people God works through, but at the source of the power. He isn’t amazed at the Red Sea splitting: God spoke creation into existence and turned words into water, so holding it back for a while is small work. He isn’t amazed at a flawed man driving a stick into the sand. He is amazed that God cares for his people in need, chose the most unimpressive misfits to be his people, and is concerned for those everyone else ignores. He could have chosen Egypt, but he chose her slaves.

Josh saw a headline about a believer whose sight was restored after baptism, and a testimony of a young woman raised in a cult whose body convulsed as evil spirits came out of her when she was baptized in Jesus’ name. Does God still do these things? Yes. Nothing is too hard for him. Why does he do them? To glorify himself, draw people to himself, and reveal himself to those whose eyes have been pulled shut.

In the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, walk.” Peter takes his right hand, his feet and ankles become strong, and he goes into the temple courts walking, jumping, and praising God. The people recognize him and are filled with wonder and amazement.
Verse 6 is the key verse: in the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, rise up and walk. The apostles healed through the Holy Spirit’s power, not their own.

On the way to Leslie’s for a bag of salt, Josh’s family came upon a car dead in the middle of the street, blocking McDonald’s, Taco Bell, and Safeway all at once. His first thought was how to get around it. He has learned that your first instinct usually isn’t the one to go with, and the next thought, park and help, was from the Lord.

A frightened teenage girl was afraid to get out of the car, and a woman trying to help couldn’t get it into neutral. They jumped it, got it into neutral, and pushed it to safety. The woman told Josh she had counted more than ten vehicles honking as they drove by, and he was the first to get out and help; after that everybody started helping. He told her Jesus had called him out on his selfishness or he would have driven by too. The Lord used it to show her Jesus and to show his son that they are the kind of people who stop in the street. We don’t need more Christian honkers.

Would he join the apostles and plant a church, or use his new freedom to build a name and a business? Josh doesn’t know.

Scripture shows a clear difference between little faith and big faith. Little faith believes when the checking account is flush, the marriage rocking, the kids thriving, the 401(k) growing. Jesus rebukes it in the disciples: they get out of the boat, but when circumstances get sketchy they doubt, and he doesn’t say, “Good job, you’re halfway there.” We can all relate: when our needs are met our faith is strong, and when we are in need, doubt sets in.

Big faith, or mature faith, stays fixed on Jesus through good and bad. Layoffs hit: God has a plan. A health scare: I don’t know what he’s doing, but I trust him. The loss of a loved one: my heart is broken, but my faith is not shaken. Big faith trusts God while the winds blow and the boat shakes.

documents.excerpt: A brother in the church, Dan, has been in the hospital almost a month fighting for his life. Before his surgery Josh prayed over him: “Heal Dan, Lord. Give us more time with this brother,” who has taught him so much about leadership, “but your will be done.” Dan, who usually gives Josh a hard time, looked at him seriously and said, “Josh, I’m not worried. This is why God allows us to suffer: so we can show a joy that can’t be shaken even in the most difficult circumstances. Everyone wants the healing, and we want to be with those we love as long as possible, but God is glorified not only in miraculous healings but in peaceful goodbyes. Dying well brings just as much glory to God as being healed. Healings make headlines, and they should, but Josh finds just as much power sitting with someone as they sing their way into the Lord’s presence. Whether healing or heaven, praise God.

documents.excerpt: Any name with this much power will bring a power struggle. In chapter 4 the priests, the captain of the temple, and the Sadducees come upon them, greatly annoyed that they are proclaiming in Jesus the resurrection of the dead. The Sadducees loved their power and status and rejected resurrection, so this is political and religious: Jesus has more power than they do, and the apostles are claiming he was raised.
excerpts: Any name with this much power will bring a power struggle. In chapter 4 the priests, the captain of the temple, and the Sadducees come upon them, greatly annoyed that they are proclaiming in Jesus the resurrection of the dead. The Sadducees loved their power and status and rejected resurrection, so this is political and religious: Jesus has more power than they do, and the apostles are claiming he was raised.

The Sadducees are a Christian comedy sketch waiting to happen. Josh pictures two of them standing at the empty tomb: “What now?” Instead of being convinced by evidence they were wrong, they ask how to bury and twist it. Their well-thought-out plan: arrest Peter and John and hold them overnight. But many who heard believed, and the men numbered about 5,000.

Jerusalem’s population was perhaps 40,000 to 45,000, only heads of households were counted, and the 3,000 from Pentecost must be added, so probably five to seven thousand. Christianity literally exploded over one long weekend in Jerusalem. Acts 2 is the birth of the church; Acts 4 is the birth of persecution. Satan starts his work immediately at the church’s first signs of success.

The Sadducees loved their power and status and rejected resurrection, so this is political and religious: Jesus has more power than they do, and the apostles are claiming he was raised.
The Sadducees are a Christian comedy sketch waiting to happen. Josh pictures two of them standing at the empty tomb: “What now?” Instead of being convinced by evidence they were wrong, they ask how to bury and twist it. Their well-thought-out plan: arrest Peter and John and hold them overnight. But many who heard believed, and the men numbered about 5,000.
Jerusalem’s population was perhaps 40,000 to 45,000, only heads of households were counted, and the 3,000 from Pentecost must be added, so probably five to seven thousand. Christianity literally exploded over one long weekend in Jerusalem. Acts 2 is the birth of the church; Acts 4 is the birth of persecution. Satan starts his work immediately at the church’s first signs of success.

excerpts: This is a massive shift in what Josh calls God’s operational strategy, which some call his redemptive plan. Before Christ, God’s presence was with the people; now it is in you. In Exodus 25 God told them to build a sanctuary where he would dwell among them. There’s a reason the room is called the auditorium and not the sanctuary: you are all sanctuaries, and this is just a building.

Paul tells the Christians in Corinth: don’t you know that you yourselves are God’s temple and that God’s Spirit dwells in your midst? We go from a temple made by man to a temple made by God. Back then they served God out of fear of what he would do if they broke the law; now we serve out of love for Jesus Christ and the power of the Spirit within us. Paul calls it a mystery.

Jesus accomplished his work, ascended, and the Father responded to his perfect obedience by sending the Spirit, who was not given until Jesus had been glorified. Christ’s work outlines what God is doing in us: his life is our righteousness by faith, his death brings pardon, his resurrection brings justification, “just as if I’d never sinned,” and his ascension makes way for the Spirit to come and give gifts. Ephesians 4: Christ gave apostles, prophets, evangelists, pastors, and teachers to equip his people until we all reach unity and maturity in Christ.

excerpts: Josh’s wife was a victim of this as a young girl. (God plans revival services, not men; he’ll leave it at that.) The children’s pastor taught that every believer can receive the gift of tongues if they believe and ask, then laid hands on the children expecting them to fall, slain in the Spirit. She fell because everyone else did; she didn’t want to be the one left standing.

His heart breaks imagining the doubt and insecurity in her mind on the floor: Was I supposed to feel something? Why did God reveal himself to my friend and not me? When is it okay to get up? Does God love me the same? Am I truly saved? The uncertainty it creates is evidence it was not from God.

Josh would take that little girl’s hand and tell her what he would tell anyone: he doesn’t know when or how God will reveal himself. For his wife, the Spirit played out not in that moment but years later, as God worked simultaneously in her future husband to prepare both hearts to come together in a marriage that displays God’s unity with his Son. You might not feel what everyone else feels, and that’s okay; keep trusting him. The movement of the Spirit you can’t see is usually the most powerful one.

documents.excerpt: Amazed and perplexed, they asked what this meant, but some made fun of them, as there are always some: they’ve had too much wine.
excerpts: Amazed and perplexed, they asked what this meant, but some made fun of them, as there are always some: they’ve had too much wine.

Josh, “just a little Baptist boy with no clue,” looked up the phrase “drunk in the Spirit,” which always confused him. He thinks of self-control when he thinks of the Spirit, because that is what Scripture teaches, and from experience he thinks of no control at all when he thinks of drunkenness. Nowhere does the Bible say to be drunk in the Spirit, and it doesn’t speak highly of being drunk at all.

Yet some leaders tell God’s people to cast off all restraint, which is not biblical, and point to slurred speech and falling to the ground as proof of the Spirit’s work. Why would the very one who gives self-control lead us to behave like drunks? Being filled with the Spirit isn’t an emotionally charged experience, a divine buzz, or a heavenly high; it is faithful, sober, reverent submission to the God of glory.

excerpts: Some twist these verses to teach that you must be baptized to be saved, or to receive the Holy Spirit. Josh says Luke destroys both in Acts. Baptism is an outward expression of an inward reality, a public declaration of how Jesus has changed your life, sharing an intimate faith with the body so they are built up and invited to celebrate what God is doing. If baptism were required for salvation, Peter would bring it up in his other letters and teaching, and he doesn’t.

The idea that you can’t receive the Spirit without baptism is easier to dismantle: read Acts 10 and tell it to the people in Cornelius’s home, who received the Spirit before they were baptized. Stop putting your expectations on God; his way, his timing. Get out of the way and pray.

We aren’t baptized to receive the Spirit or to be saved; we are baptized because we are saved and want to obey, and because Jesus’ baptism so pleased God that the skies opened, the Spirit came down like a dove, and he declared, “This is my Son.” As his adopted sons and daughters, all we want is to please him. If baptism were required for salvation, none of the people listed in Hebrews 11 would be saved either.

documents.excerpt: The central point of the apostles’ teaching was that salvation is a gift from God: you didn’t make it happen; Jesus did it for you. That is why you can go through all the toil of life with a smile: you hold a gift that compares to no other.
excerpts: The central point of the apostles’ teaching was that salvation is a gift from God: you didn’t make it happen; Jesus did it for you. That is why you can go through all the toil of life with a smile: you hold a gift that compares to no other.

The world says everything you need is within you. Christianity says nothing you have matters if you don’t have Jesus, because something is wrong with all our hearts. You aren’t unhappy because you married an idiot or your boss is a jerk; something in you needs to be transformed and your mind renewed, by devoting yourself daily to God’s word and to relationship with Jesus.

Growing Christians are students of the word. If you don’t like to read, buy headphones and get an audio Bible or a C. S. Lewis audiobook. Talk to people who know more than you; if they are jerks about it, Josh will knock them down a peg. Memorize Scripture, read with your family, hang it on your walls and doorframes, sign your kids up for Kids Truth on Wednesday nights, and join a life group, as Chris said.

No: start your own. “I don’t get a lot out of it.” Life groups weren’t launched so you could get a lot out of them, but so you could pour a lot out; you empty yourself and are filled in the emptying.

The early church responded to Christ’s sacrifice by sacrificing for each other; it was contagious, which is why it was unstoppable. What better way to love God than to love your neighbor? “I love Jesus, I just can’t stand his people” is a cute line, but there are no excuses: God didn’t ask you to like your neighbor; he said to love him. Jesus didn’t wait for you to be lovable; he loved you first. Go and do the same.

excerpts: They sold property and possessions for anyone in need and put it all on the line for each other. That is why the church talks about giving as sacrifice, not tithes, numbers, and percentages.

Some numbskull always says Jesus was a socialist. documents.excerpt: In Josh’s opinion 2020 was the hardest year to oversee the church ever. A few, like John MacArthur, insisted the world needed the church doors open, but there was tremendous fear inside and outside the church, and fear caused a lot of mistakes.
excerpts: In Josh’s opinion 2020 was the hardest year to oversee the church ever. A few, like John MacArthur, insisted the world needed the church doors open, but there was tremendous fear inside and outside the church, and fear caused a lot of mistakes.

Josh admits he led like a coward during Covid: he went along with everything, preached to empty rooms and said nothing, ran to get tested, reported who he had breathed on, and kept his distance. He isn’t proud of that period. The email reminded him how churches and the culture isolated the sick to preserve everyone else, shamed people for coming to worship with a mild cough, and fought over masks and vaccines. The capital-C church didn’t speak truth or unity into the divide; it made it worse, and he was part of that.

The church stopped being the church because the government said it was unsafe. Being the true church is never unsafe. If green stuff is coming out of your nose and you’re running 104, stay home and rest, but we shouldn’t avoid, shame, or isolate ourselves from you; we should bring you soup. He dredges up these sour memories because when we make mistakes we have a duty to own them and learn from them.

2020: when the church stopped being the church
In Josh’s opinion 2020 was the hardest year to oversee the church ever. A few, like John MacArthur, insisted the world needed the church doors open, but there was tremendous fear inside and outside the church, and fear caused a lot of mistakes.
Josh admits he led like a coward during Covid: he went along with everything, preached to empty rooms and said nothing, ran to get tested, reported who he had breathed on, and kept his distance. He isn’t proud of that period. The email reminded him how churches and the culture isolated the sick to preserve everyone else, shamed people for coming to worship with a mild cough, and fought over masks and vaccines. The capital-C church didn’t speak truth or unity into the divide; it made it worse, and he was part of that.
The church stopped being the church because the government said it was unsafe. Being the true church is never unsafe. If green stuff is coming out of your nose and you’re running 104, stay home and rest, but we shouldn’t avoid, shame, or isolate ourselves from you; we should bring you soup. excerpts: Each new series starts with genre: Genesis is history, Leviticus law, Proverbs wisdom, Psalms poetry, Isaiah and Jeremiah prophecy, Matthew and Luke gospel narratives, Romans an epistle, and Acts history. The bigger argument is whether Acts is prescriptive, telling us what to do, or descriptive, telling us what God did in a specific place and time. Josh says yes: a little of both.

If you want to argue it is 100 percent prescriptive, keep reading: at the end of chapter 1, after Judas’s betrayal, the apostles choose between Joseph and Matthias by praying and casting lots, and the lot falls to Matthias. How would you feel if that was how the church chose elders or children’s workers? “You guys look suitable; let’s grab some dice.”

That part is descriptive; we have other ways to determine whether someone is qualified. Prayer, careful study, and discernment uncover whether something is prescriptive or descriptive. Some parts are obviously meant to be applied, which becomes clear as we compare them with other Scripture; other parts simply tell you what happened.

There is moral power: qualities that set us apart, gentleness with courage and conviction, intense passion with deep patience, honesty, goodness, kindness, and charity. And there is spiritual power, the fruit of the Spirit described as self-control, which makes the believer a strong influence: confident, ready to speak at a moment’s notice, bold when what they say isn’t what people want to hear, humble and transparent, disliking sin in themselves more than in others.

Meek is the word that keeps coming to mind: not weakness but confident humility. It is attractive; it makes people pause and ask what is different about this person, which would come in handy for a community spreading the gospel to the ends of the earth.

excerpts: When this power lands on a person it bears fruit, and it isn’t a difficult labor but one filled with joy and praise. The key to happiness isn’t what you acquire but who acquires you; the Holy Spirit is the source of Christian joy.

Josh thinks of his son Nolan, one of his best friends at 10. They do everything together; Nolan feels safe and Josh feels useful. Discipline stinks, but afterward Josh can hold him and tell him how much he loves him; after a bad day or a bad grade he can reassure and encourage him. Nolan will always be his son and Josh always his daddy. The confidence Nolan has that Josh has his back is the confidence Josh has that the Lord has his.

He walks down the street singing, “Oh, how he loves us.” “But Josh, have you even seen him? Did you see him on the cross? Did you see him walk out of the tomb?” No. “Then how do you know he loves you?” “I just do.” His heart is so full of God’s love that he has extra for people he doesn’t even know. That is what it is like to be clothed with power from on high.

excerpts: Josh takes a page from Peter and John’s playbook before the Sanhedrin. The authorities say, in effect, your services are getting loud, the gospel is a little intrusive, could you back off? Peter and John answer: which is right in God’s eyes, to listen to you or to him? You be the judges; as for us, we cannot help speaking about what we have seen and heard. Will you be quiet, please? No.

If you have seen and believe in Christ, you must speak of Christ, and if anyone, even the government, asks you not to, you must not listen. As Peter later writes in 1 Peter 3: in your hearts revere Christ as Lord, always be prepared to give an answer for the hope you have, with gentleness and respect.

Effective witnesses always begin as his students: they read, study, memorize, and learn the doctrine taught by the apostles, then present the facts with confidence from the power they’ve been clothed with, and with respect and love.

excerpts: We can always grow as witnesses, but there are also ways to become less effective, and this might sting: how Christians live affects the believability of their witness. A drug addict or convicted felon isn’t your best witness in a murder trial; haven’t you watched Law & Order? A lawyer in the church told Josh that if a jury thinks a witness lied about anything, they wonder if the witness is lying about everything.

Homework: read Titus 2. In verse 10, in the NIV, our goal is to make the teaching about God our Savior attractive. We are salesmen; our product is the truth and the gospel, and our direct report is God. Paul tells Titus to set an example by doing what is good, with integrity, seriousness, and soundness of speech, so that those who oppose you may be ashamed because they have nothing bad to say about us.

The opposite is true too: if people can say all kinds of bad about you while you’re outspoken as a Christian, you dishonor the word of God, and the Christian is put to shame instead of the opponent, which hurts the momentum, growth, and health of the church. To help God save a lost world, we must be sanctified and work to rid our lives of sin. Nothing is worse than a salesman uninterested in his product, pitching a Mercedes while driving a Camry. Witnesses can’t run around looking like they did before they knew him.

Josh was full of darkness and pride, drowning in sin, selfish; he caused many people pain, took what wasn’t his, and gave nothing away. He was a fool, and sometimes that guy still rears his ugly head. But he heard the words of Jesus, and keeps coming back to them: come to me, all you who are weary and burdened, and I will give you rest; take my yoke upon you and learn from me, for I am gentle and humble in heart; my yoke is easy and my burden is light. Josh was a drunk, swearing, pleasure-chasing addict and idiot, and God melted his heart. He used to love those things and now hates them. He used to mock Christians as dorky, weak nerds; now he looks up to them and is proud of their faith, persistence, hope, joy, and confidence. He wishes people had known him 15 or 20 years ago: he isn’t the man he was. He isn’t perfect, but he has been transformed, and all he did was rest and sit at the Master’s feet.

Jesus sustains him every day, pulls him out of bad patterns, reminds him of his word, his goodness, how far he has come and where he is going, leads him away from temptation, and makes clear what he does and doesn’t want for him. This confidence, joy, freedom, hope, passion, and transformation is what the church was launched on. Josh finds no greater joy than walking with Jesus, and hopes everyone has it too.

excerpts: This is the final week of Misquoted, and Chris gives a quick review whether everyone likes it or not. Week one: “Jesus says not to judge,” which Josh did a wonderful job showing has been misquoted. Week two: “Follow your heart.” Chris has followed his heart right off a cliff; his feelings didn’t work out so well.

Week three: “God won’t give you more than you can handle.” Chris has always thought we got one word wrong: it should say God won’t give you more than he can handle. Chris has had more than he can handle many times, but in his weakness God’s grace was sufficient and his power was made perfect.

Week four: “I can be perfect if I try.” If someone says they can be perfect because the Holy Spirit is in them, Chris wants to interview those closest to them: spouse, kids, co-workers, best friends. He does not give permission to interview the people in his life, because he would hate for anyone to find out he wasn’t always wonderful, kind, gentle, and loving.

excerpts: Chris isn’t saying words aren’t powerful; he will get to their true power. But we do not create or manifest things with our words. Creation is reserved solely for the Creator God, who created with his words.

In Genesis 1, verses 3, 6, 9, 14, and 24, each day of creation starts with “And God said,” followed by “Let there be”: let there be lights, let the water teem with living creatures, let the land produce living creatures. On the sixth day, “Then God said, ‘Let us make mankind.’” God spoke and creation just happened. Chris wishes he had been there.

We are made in his image, but we are not little gods. Verse 28 is where mankind got its marching orders: be fruitful and increase in number, fill the earth and subdue it, rule over the fish, the birds, and every living creature. If God intended us to create, he would have given us that mandate at creation; creating is reserved for God alone.

Matthew 6:24: no one can serve two masters; you cannot serve both God and money. If our minds are on our health, wealth, and happiness, they aren’t centered on Christ; we must devote ourselves to being sanctified and looking more like our Savior.

Since when have sinful humans known what is truly best for ourselves? Isn’t that why we turned to Christ in the first place, because our way wasn’t working? (“How’s that working out for you?” Thanks, Dr. Phil.) God calls us to give up our desires and replace them with his. 1 John 2: do not love the world; the lust of the flesh, the lust of the eyes, and the pride of life come not from the Father. Matthew 6: store up treasures in heaven, for where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.

Bottom line: if we are worried about health, wealth, and happiness and buy into a doctrine that says we can create whatever we want, our focus is not on Christ. We are striving in the wrong direction and need to change course.

documents.excerpt: Have you met someone who hasn’t been through anything difficult yet, no lost loved one or job, even met their spouse in high school with no bad breakup? Chris isn’t making fun; you might be in here, and the tough stuff will hit, but it hasn’t yet.
excerpts: Have you met someone who hasn’t been through anything difficult yet, no lost loved one or job, even met their spouse in high school with no bad breakup? Chris isn’t making fun; you might be in here, and the tough stuff will hit, but it hasn’t yet.

He has noticed two things about such friends. First, they have no idea how to walk others through tough times; they mean well, but they reach for platitudes like “God works everything for good” or “It’ll all work out in the end.” Second, when something finally turned their life upside down, the blessing was having others who knew that pain walk through it with them.

If Christians never walked through trials or pain, we would have no idea how to care for the hurting in a world full of pain, and imagine how shallow our faith would be if it were never tested. Chris concludes the thought with Romans 5: we glory in our sufferings, because suffering produces perseverance, perseverance character, and character hope, and hope does not put us to shame. We have hope because of it.

excerpts: Chris has shown that name it and claim it isn’t what Scripture teaches, but he doesn’t want to leave it there. The power of the tongue is real, just in a different way than creating.

Back to James, in James 3: bits in horses’ mouths turn the whole animal; a very small rudder steers a large ship; a great forest is set on fire by a small spark. The tongue is a fire, a world of evil that corrupts the whole body; no human being can tame it. With it we praise our Lord and Father and curse human beings made in God’s likeness. Can fresh water and salt water flow from the same spring?

Simply put, our mouth steers us and can corrupt our whole body. Believers should take serious stock of what comes out of their mouths, even in jest. Are we using words to build up or tear down, to praise the Lord or to curse? According to James, it is probably both, and as James says, that shouldn’t be.

excerpts: Why do our words mean so much? What comes out of your mouth is what is in your heart; Chris’s too.

You can pretend all day that the dirty jokes, the cuss words, or tearing others down “all in good fun” are just words and not who you truly are, but the word of God says that’s a lie. We are what comes out of our mouth.

Chris really likes the way the ESV puts it: “Out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaks.” What we speak isn’t the dark corners of our heart; it is the abundance of our heart. Whatever is coming out of your mouth is what you are filling your heart with.

documents.context: Josh Wyatt · August 4, 2024 · Misquoted
documents.excerpt: Expectations are the ultimate relationship builder and the ultimate relationship killer. Properly communicated and properly answered, they build trust and deepen relationships: “I need this from you.” “Okay, I understand; let me work on that.”
excerpts: Expectations are the ultimate relationship builder and the ultimate relationship killer. Properly communicated and properly answered, they build trust and deepen relationships: “I need this from you.” “Okay, I understand; let me work on that.”

When they aren’t communicated or responded to properly, they break trust and make relationships so fragile that sharing your deepest thoughts becomes a horrifying endeavor. Josh voices the unspoken version: “You should know I need this from you,” and until you figure it out, anger, resentment, and bitterness grow. “How dare you not know my deepest insecurities… my hidden and unspoken desires.”
He wishes he could slap a “Handle With Care” sticker on everyone’s expectations. Whether in a friendship, a marriage, or a pastor and his congregation, communicating expectations is vital.

excerpts: In verse 13 Jesus moves to difficult concepts: you are the salt of the earth, but if the salt loses its saltiness it is good for nothing but to be thrown out and trampled.

Salt in Palestine, especially around the Dead Sea, was contaminated with gypsum and other minerals until it wasn’t really salt anymore, and in the home it would be thrown out. Jesus isn’t saying, as many teach, that you can lose your salvation, but that you can lose your effectiveness in leading others to salvation, the purpose for which you were created. The world can contaminate you until your word carries no weight and you aren’t believable or trustworthy.

On murder: you have heard it said, you shall not murder, but anyone who is angry with a brother or sister will be subject to judgment. excerpts: Here is the misquote: many Christians wrongly assume that because Jesus saved us from our sins, we will no longer struggle and wrestle with our sinfulness. That is unfortunate and false.

Two crowds form around the command to be perfect. Some press back on Jesus: why command what he knows we can’t do? Easy: he wants you to rely on him to do it. As Jesus would later teach, with human beings this is impossible, but with God all things are possible. If God gives a command, he provides the power to accomplish it; he isn’t cruel, setting a mark you can’t reach and laughing as you try.

Human righteousness is possible: just be better than the guy next to you. Because it is so reachable, it is like filthy rags in God’s eyes. God’s righteousness is impossible: just be equal to God in all things. That is why it is holy and perfect. But the impossible mark becomes possible for anyone who trusts in Jesus, because he gives them his righteousness; as it is written, the righteous will live by faith.

documents.excerpt: Josh illustrates it on stage. Jesus commands us to be perfect, and we answer, “That’s not possible, so I’ll do this instead,” and change the target to one with a huge bullseye. “Now I’m feeling confident. Look, Ma.” It seems ridiculous pointed out, but it is common, and because we do it we stop caring about hitting the mark he laid out and only worry about getting closer than the next person.
excerpts: Josh illustrates it on stage. Jesus commands us to be perfect, and we answer, “That’s not possible, so I’ll do this instead,” and change the target to one with a huge bullseye. “Now I’m feeling confident. Look, Ma.” It seems ridiculous pointed out, but it is common, and because we do it we stop caring about hitting the mark he laid out and only worry about getting closer than the next person.

It sounds like this: “I’m a pretty honest person, definitely more trustworthy than her.” “Yeah, I look at porn, but at least I’m not running out on her.” “Yeah, I have a bad temper, but I’d never hurt anyone.” But the Christian goal isn’t to be better than them; it is to be like him.

Jesus points to his target: that’s it; aim for that. When you miss, not if but when, confess it to God and to everyone you hit in the process, and Jesus grabs the axe and says, “Try again.” The believer’s power isn’t in the accuracy of the throw but in the freedom to try again, and again.

Jesus wants you to see your inability to hit the mark every time, which leads to the meek and poor attitudes of the Beatitudes, often called spiritual bankruptcy. You need divine assistance to reach the divine standard.

Josh describes sitting around a table with godly men he respects and does life with, men who love Jesus, fall short, ask for forgiveness, and walk in grace upon grace, when one man, with a witness he brought along, says he no longer sins. “It’s weird.” Josh has witnessed the claim only once, and once was enough.

The false doctrine of sinless perfection isn’t widespread, but it is worth addressing so the church is prepared to answer biblically. Achieving moral perfection is actually a great goal; God commands it. But to say you’ve achieved it is another matter.

You expect a newborn on a bottle for a while, but not a five-year-old walking around with one; eventually the child eats solid food. You expect the child who throws bedtime tantrums to eventually handle the routine: “Go brush your teeth and go to bed. Get out my face.” (Just kidding.)
In Matthew 5 Jesus is clearly raising the bar: aren’t even tax collectors doing that? If you only say hi to your homies, don’t the pagans do that? The kingdom of God doesn’t look like the world, and there is greater responsibility as you grow in the faith: be perfect, therefore, as your heavenly Father is perfect.
documents.title: What perfectionism gets right — Expectations

documents.excerpt: The Lord expects more of us because Christians make big claims, and a claim that something has happened to you should be supported with strong evidence.
excerpts: The Lord expects more of us because Christians make big claims, and a claim that something has happened to you should be supported with strong evidence.

The Christian claims to be a new creation, and the skeptic asks, “Oh, really? What’s new about you?” The Christian claims to be awakened to the evil of sin: “Is there less of it in your life?” The Christian claims Jesus rescued them: “Do you have more joy than before? Why do you only go to church once a month?” The Christian claims eternal rewards and a crown in heaven: “Are they telling other people how to get there?”

If you say you’ve received it, your life should provide proof. Claiming to be an adopted child of God while living in unholiness is the greatest hypocrisy; Peter says many will bring the way of truth into disrepute, and you slander the name of God. If you are a new creation being made holy, show it: let your light shine before others, that they may see your good deeds and glorify your Father in heaven. If you are still your old self, stop claiming to be a new creation.

documents.excerpt: Every believer in Christ is born again: not a make-believe Christian idea but a true, living experience. We have gone from death to life, and God dwells in us by his Spirit.
excerpts: Every believer in Christ is born again: not a make-believe Christian idea but a true, living experience. We have gone from death to life, and God dwells in us by his Spirit.

Jesus told the Pharisee Nicodemus that no one can see the kingdom of God without being born again. Nicodemus was confused, thinking about a second trip through the birth canal, but this isn’t like the first birth. The second birth begins something new; the new life produces good fruit, more than the previous life. The expectations are higher, but in Christ we are enabled to reach further than ever before.

That is why a believer can never say, “Josh, you don’t understand, there’s no way I can drop that habit or kick that addiction.” You have the Spirit of God in you, the third person of the Trinity; God is all-powerful, so how can you set a cap on his power in your life? We can burn down addictions, tear down idols, take our sin out back, shoot it, bury it, and never see it again. God gives us victory through Jesus Christ.

Everyone who hears these words and puts them into practice is like a wise man who built his house on the rock; the rain, streams, and winds beat against it, yet it did not fall. documents.excerpt: Today is week three of the five-week series Misquoted, looking at texts often twisted out of context, sometimes innocently, so that God’s word is misused, misapplied, and misquoted.
excerpts: Today is week three of the five-week series Misquoted, looking at texts often twisted out of context, sometimes innocently, so that God’s word is misused, misapplied, and misquoted.

In week one, many Christians had taken Matthew 7, where Jesus teaches us how to judge rightly, as a command never to judge anyone for anything. That can’t be true, because Scripture consistently calls believers to kill sin in their own lives, which is one way we love God, and to help others do the same, which is one way we love our neighbor. Knowing God’s view of sin and its consequences, how loving would it be to let another drown in it? We are ordered to be loving truth tellers who listen to our own sermons before we preach them.

As a warm-up before the real deal, Josh notes how many grab that phrase and make massive claims like “God loves you just the way you are.” That is what Satan does: he takes a truth and inserts a dab of deception so it still sounds good.
excerpts: Many misquotes could have made the series. One is from 1 John 4:8, where John simply states that God is love. As a warm-up before the real deal, Josh notes how many grab that phrase and make massive claims like “God loves you just the way you are.” That is what Satan does: he takes a truth and inserts a dab of deception so it still sounds good.

Josh suspects some actually mean that love is God: whatever or whoever we love is God, and you’d better show proper respect. Many shove God into the box of their experiences with human love, as though he is just a father with a software update, Father 2.0. Please don’t. God describes his own love and doesn’t need your help; if you shape it, you’ll miss its eternal, divine, unmatched, unconditional character. Don’t shape his love; read of his love and become a scholar of it.

Yes, God loves you no matter where you are, where you come from, or what you’ve done, but you make a grave mistake if you think he intends to leave you as he found you. He loves who he created you to be and will wash all this stuff off, if you’ll let him, so you can look like him.

God doesn’t open for anyone; he is the main event. Nothing is too hard for the Lord, but that doesn’t mean he desires to bring you wealth, health, or success. documents.context: Josh Wyatt · July 28, 2024 · Misquoted
documents.excerpt: In Matthew 19 Jesus is responding to a man who asked, “Good teacher, what must I do to inherit eternal life?” He already had a successful business and everything else, and he set his eyes on eternal life not because he wanted heaven’s treasures but because he wanted his earthly treasures never to fade. Jesus told him to sell everything, give to the poor, and come follow him, and he went away sad, because he knew it was going to end.
excerpts: In Matthew 19 Jesus is responding to a man who asked, “Good teacher, what must I do to inherit eternal life?” He already had a successful business and everything else, and he set his eyes on eternal life not because he wanted heaven’s treasures but because he wanted his earthly treasures never to fade. Jesus told him to sell everything, give to the poor, and come follow him, and he went away sad, because he knew it was going to end.

Jesus was explaining that salvation is impossible for humans to acquire by works: with human beings this is impossible, but with God all things are possible. Jesus isn’t your dream catcher, golden goose, co-pilot, sixth man, cheerleader, or right-hand man; he is your Lord and Savior, Master and friend, fighting for your soul, not your success.

So many misquotes happen when people forget Christianity isn’t just about how to live now but how to live forever. Jesus isn’t part of your story; by his great mercy you are part of his. Praise God, he did the impossible by saving you from death and hell through his death and resurrection.

excerpts: In 1 Corinthians, Paul has just pointed to himself as a mature Christian, not arrogantly but to teach, saying self-discipline and self-control are crucial to serving God better. Then in chapter 10 he uses Israel’s history as an example of immaturity: no humility, no self-control, overconfidence. Paul good, Israel bad.

It is simple: no believer can claim they were overpowered by temptation. “The devil made me do it”? No, he didn’t. You had a way out and chose to do it. Satan can’t even make an unbeliever sin; do you think he has more power over you as a believer? You sinned because you were willing to.
That is the problem with the misquote: in 1 Corinthians 10 Paul is writing about temptation, not suffering, so using a verse on temptation to comfort someone dealing with loss misses it.

documents.excerpt: Josh remembers the exact moment, while overcoming addiction, that he first experienced Paul’s way out. Until then all he had ever seen was the way in; he never looked for a way out or knew there was one. He just took the bait.
excerpts: Josh remembers the exact moment, while overcoming addiction, that he first experienced Paul’s way out. Until then all he had ever seen was the way in; he never looked for a way out or knew there was one. He just took the bait.

That day he felt like a catfish floating by a log under the surface, eyeing the shiny worm of temptation. For the first time, instead of chomping down and ending up gutted, breaded, and dipped in hot oil, he paused, prayed, and walked away. He looked up and asked, “God, what do you think?” and realized he already knew. So he asked, “God, can you help me walk away from this? I keep hearing about this power you have. Do you have it? Because I need some.” Now he knows what it looks like; he and God are dangerous together, eliminating sin in his life, and he has proof of a strength he didn’t think he had.

documents.context: Josh Wyatt · July 28, 2024 · Misquoted
documents.excerpt: So don’t be shocked by older believers who are immature: they refused to surrender to the process. If you won’t open your life and God’s word and let him command you like a platoon leader, don’t be surprised when he never sends you on a special mission.
excerpts: So don’t be shocked by older believers who are immature: they refused to surrender to the process. If you won’t open your life and God’s word and let him command you like a platoon leader, don’t be surprised when he never sends you on a special mission.

God spent 25 years working in Abraham before blessing him with Isaac, 13 years sending trials to Joseph before he went from prison to second in command in Egypt, and 80 years preparing Moses, a slow learner; God can use slow learners too. Jesus was with the disciples three short years before trusting them with the message that changed the world. Some take longer, and Josh is a slow learner; some serve longer or in different areas; some sit on thrones and some get hit with stones. Whoever you are, you must surrender your will and embrace the process, or gripe and complain like a child. After today you can’t say no one told you.

God wants your heart, your obedience, and your transformation. He wants you to look like Jesus in the Garden of Gethsemane, resting beneath his will: “God, I don’t think I want this, but I want what you want more.” Mature believers rest in his will. They aren’t driven by emotions or swayed by fancy new thinking; they patiently await Christ’s arrival and consider everything joy in the meantime, because they know how it ends.

God spent 25 years working in Abraham before blessing him with Isaac, 13 years sending trials to Joseph before he went from prison to second in command in Egypt, and 80 years preparing Moses, a slow learner; God can use slow learners too. Jesus was with the disciples three short years before trusting them with the message that changed the world. Some take longer, and Josh is a slow learner; some serve longer or in different areas; some sit on thrones and some get hit with stones. Whoever you are, you must surrender your will and embrace the process, or gripe and complain like a child. After today you can’t say no one told you.
God wants your heart, your obedience, and your transformation. He wants you to look like Jesus in the Garden of Gethsemane, resting beneath his will: “God, I don’t think I want this, but I want what you want more.” Mature believers rest in his will. They aren’t driven by emotions or swayed by fancy new thinking; they patiently await Christ’s arrival and consider everything joy in the meantime, because they know how it ends.

excerpts: Josh loves Coach Taylor’s game-day line in Friday Night Lights: “Clear eyes, full hearts, can’t lose.” Believer, you can’t lose unless you give up. He challenges the church to reclaim some ground for the kingdom today and let God get back to work on them. He doesn’t care where you’re coming from or what you came in with; he cares what you go out with. Invite God to make a mess of what you’ve built, tear it down, and build something new.

Immediately the devil starts: it’s too late, you’re too far gone, why fix this, you’ve got a good life, you earned it. Josh gives permission to defy his lies, be a rebel, be a maverick. There’s a reason you’re here, and it isn’t because you have it all figured out. Get up, get to work, don’t look back, and let him finish his work in you.

This is the Christian grind: faithfulness day after day, surrenders, bumps, and bruises, with unrelenting hope in the one who saves us, changes us, and sends us. Every day is a series of choices between the right way and the easy way, and we keep our eye on the narrow road. Jesus didn’t do easy or comfortable, so neither do we. When you let the King rule your life, it isn’t the end but the beginning, and it only gets harder. Satan gets more satisfaction the farther you’ve come when you fall on your face, but he has no answer to grace. So stay vigilant, be patient with the process, and do not lose heart.

excerpts: Steve gave his life to Jesus at nine years old, 60 years ago this week, and has loved Jesus every single day since. Yet on the living sacrifice part he has logged a lot of miles falling off his altar and climbing back up. By the silence, he guesses he’s the only one.

Some climb God’s altar, then get scared it isn’t mercy and God will zap them, so they run for the hills. Some fear God will tire of their lousy track record and vaporize them, so they sneak down the back side hoping he won’t notice. Others stay but keep juking to be a moving target, or keep one foot on the ground for a fast getaway. Steve was never a horrible infidel, just a fairly decent guy, but there were times he could have used an escalator on his altar, offering his body to God only temporarily, for the same reason you slip off yours.

documents.excerpt: The big, out-of-control pattern these days is the personal identity movement: this is how I identify, therefore this must be who I am. The apostle John encountered a similar pattern 2,000 years ago, and it sounds current: do not love the world, for everything in the world, the cravings of sinful man (you are what you have), the lust of his eyes (you are what you do), and the boasting of what he has and does (you are what people say you are), comes not from the Father but from the world.
excerpts: The big, out-of-control pattern these days is the personal identity movement: this is how I identify, therefore this must be who I am. The apostle John encountered a similar pattern 2,000 years ago, and it sounds current: do not love the world, for everything in the world, the cravings of sinful man (you are what you have), the lust of his eyes (you are what you do), and the boasting of what he has and does (you are what people say you are), comes not from the Father but from the world.

Every day our minds are bombarded by sights and sounds designed to appeal to sinful cravings, lustful appetites, and pride, producing desires that want us to act out. That is the pattern: look at images that feed my ego, think about engaging with them, think enough that I want to, until ultimately I do. That’s why Paul is emphatic: don’t go there; don’t be Jell-O; don’t be conformed to the predictable, unreliable thinking that has landed you in so many ditches.

Every day our minds are bombarded by sights and sounds designed to appeal to sinful cravings, lustful appetites, and pride, producing desires that want us to act out. That is the pattern: look at images that feed my ego, think about engaging with them, think enough that I want to, until ultimately I do. That’s why Paul is emphatic: don’t go there; don’t be Jell-O; don’t be conformed to the predictable, unreliable thinking that has landed you in so many ditches.
documents.title: The pattern of this world — Therefore, This is Who I Am!

excerpts: Before anyone writes him: Steve believes God almost exclusively speaks through his written word. But when you fill your mind with God’s mind and are willing to listen, he will speak, not audibly, but those with ears to hear will hear loud and clear.

What he heard was a simple question that shook him: “Steve, is Romans 8:28 still in the Bible?” He paused, and it came again. He answered out loud, feebly: “Yes, Lord, I suppose it is.” Romans 8:28 says that in all things God works for the good of those who love him, who have been called according to his purpose. “So you’re saying that verse is still in there? Huh. Still in mine too.”

“Look, son, from time to time really bad things happen, and they seem to happen to you a lot, and this one is about as bad as it gets. Go ahead and grieve, but not as others who have no hope.” In other words, don’t just follow your heart; fill your mind with God’s mind, because that’s the only way your heart will see what your eyes cannot.

documents.excerpt: One of the hardest parts of Josh’s job is knowing that the stage, lights, cameras, and boldness can make it seem he is coming from a place of superiority. There is nothing superior about him; the only thing worth boasting in is that Christ saved him and lives in him.
excerpts: One of the hardest parts of Josh’s job is knowing that the stage, lights, cameras, and boldness can make it seem he is coming from a place of superiority. There is nothing superior about him; the only thing worth boasting in is that Christ saved him and lives in him.

He would be a bum of a husband without God’s word and Spirit, a trash father without his heavenly Father showing him how to love, protect, discipline, and care, and still an addict without God’s grace patching him up time and again. Christ makes better husbands and better daddies. He isn’t a seminary saint with fancy language; he is a guy who loves Jesus, called to boast in the cross until he dies.

He stands next to legends like Paul, who gave their lives to preserve the gospel, and joins him in declaring, “I have been crucified with Christ and I no longer live, but Christ lives in me… if righteousness could be gained through the law, Christ died for nothing.” He clings to grace like the last parachute on a diving plane.

Every week he comes up humbled and amazed that God let him lead his church. He has wrestled with the word all week and been pruned first, and he prays the church carries that pruning to spouses, families, neighbors, and co-workers, and is faithful to speak when opportunities come.

documents.excerpt: Before getting into it, Josh wants to test the foundation. Brace yourself: the holy Scriptures are not about you. In our culture it is hard to believe anything isn’t about you, but trust him, it’s better this way.
excerpts: Before getting into it, Josh wants to test the foundation. Brace yourself: the holy Scriptures are not about you. In our culture it is hard to believe anything isn’t about you, but trust him, it’s better this way.

He could argue much of the church growth movement of the ’80s, ’90s, and early 2000s came from preaching built around you, tailored to make you feel like God’s special treasure child: his plans are only missing you; he wants to lavish you with every earthly blessing; live your best life now; everything happens for a reason, even your choice of toilet paper. It felt like Uncle Sam’s “We want you.” He gets why people flock to it; it’s nice to feel important, accepted, and needed. But just because it feels good doesn’t make it right.

God’s word speaks to you and sometimes addresses you directly, but it isn’t about you. You aren’t the hero God has been missing; his hero put in work 2,000 years ago on Calvary. The Bible is about Jesus: how he lived, died, and was raised for you, good news of grace for sinners.

documents.context: Josh Wyatt · July 14, 2024 · Misquoted
documents.excerpt: Misquoting Scripture doesn’t always come from a bad place; sometimes it does, and the series will probably come back to that. Some comes from an innocent place: a well-meaning life group leader reads the text and asks, “What does that mean to you?” Now everyone is empowered to interpret Scripture by how it makes them feel. Boom: misquoted.
excerpts: Misquoting Scripture doesn’t always come from a bad place; sometimes it does, and the series will probably come back to that. Some comes from an innocent place: a well-meaning life group leader reads the text and asks, “What does that mean to you?” Now everyone is empowered to interpret Scripture by how it makes them feel. Boom: misquoted.

In a good life group no one cares what you think it means; they care what it actually means. They ask who wrote it, why, when, to whom, and what the cultural setting was. To take it further, ask the genre. Josh polls the hip-hop fans and declares country the best genre, then asks: is it narrative, like Matthew, where today’s first misquoted text is; poetry, like Psalms or Proverbs; or history, like Joshua, which the church just spent seven weeks on?

His Bible school theology professor barked before every three-hour lecture: “Context, context, context.” A verse is surrounded by verses, in a chapter, in a book, that help you understand it. Chapters and verses didn’t always exist; they help with quoting and sharing, but that is also the problem: you can grab one and throw it out.

documents.excerpt: Just because you quote something from the Bible doesn’t mean it’s biblical. First Kings 11:3 says Solomon had 700 wives and 300 concubines; in Luke 10 Jesus says “Go and do likewise,” and the polygamist rejoices. People actually do this: “Well, it’s in the Bible.” So is my bookmark. Where in the Bible? Who wrote it, to whom, for what purpose? Most of the time the context is in the very next verse; just keep reading.
excerpts: Just because you quote something from the Bible doesn’t mean it’s biblical. First Kings 11:3 says Solomon had 700 wives and 300 concubines; in Luke 10 Jesus says “Go and do likewise,” and the polygamist rejoices. People actually do this: “Well, it’s in the Bible.” So is my bookmark. Where in the Bible? Who wrote it, to whom, for what purpose? Most of the time the context is in the very next verse; just keep reading.
Anyone who removes a text from its context is trying to make the verse reinforce what they want to be true. That is dangerous: instead of conforming to his words, we seek to conform his words to us.

“But Josh, Solomon was the wisest man who ever lived and had many wives.” That’s your argument? His life was a mess; his wives led him astray, and with each one he was less devoted to the Lord, because the model from creation was one woman and one man becoming one flesh for one life.

documents.excerpt: Jesus claims he is the fulfillment of all Scripture. In Luke 4 he goes to the synagogue in Nazareth, is handed the scroll of Isaiah, and reads, “The Spirit of the Lord is on me, because he has anointed me to proclaim good news to the poor… to proclaim the year of the Lord’s favor.” He rolls up the scroll, sits down with every eye on him, and says, “Today this scripture is fulfilled in your hearing.” I am the one Isaiah wrote about eight centuries earlier.
excerpts: Jesus claims he is the fulfillment of all Scripture. In Luke 4 he goes to the synagogue in Nazareth, is handed the scroll of Isaiah, and reads, “The Spirit of the Lord is on me, because he has anointed me to proclaim good news to the poor… to proclaim the year of the Lord’s favor.” He rolls up the scroll, sits down with every eye on him, and says, “Today this scripture is fulfilled in your hearing.” I am the one Isaiah wrote about eight centuries earlier.

Don’t get it twisted: the Bible isn’t a self-help book to make your life better. It is about Jesus, the only one who can make your life better. And here is the comfort: his mission is to redeem us. Scripture points to Jesus, and Jesus brings us back to God. I was lost but now I’m found; his blood washed away my sins; his resurrection guarantees my future; by grace through faith in Christ alone we are his adopted sons and daughters, given new birth into a living hope and an inheritance that can never perish, spoil, or fade.

That is why this series matters: Josh wants to know the one who saved him, walk with him, and be like him, as he wanted to be like his dad. He is drawn to the Scriptures not because they offer eternal life but because they tell him about the one who did. He can sit under Jesus’ teaching, become his disciple, drop his nets, and fish for men like Peter.

The first misquoted verse is Matthew 7: “Do not judge, or you too will be judged.” It is misquoted inside and outside the church. Unbelievers use it as a Christian chokehold: try to talk to someone about their sin and they say, “Doesn’t your God teach you not to judge?” If you aren’t equipped you might say, “I guess you’re right.”
Our culture loves it because it doesn’t want to be told what to believe or how to act. You’d think the church would stand strong and influence the culture, but that mindset has leaked in and infected the church.

documents.context: Josh Wyatt · July 14, 2024 · Misquoted
documents.excerpt: On one end, judge means to evaluate, discern, or observe: this is good, this is bad, this tastes good, this sounds horrible. Is Jesus forbidding evaluations, criticism, or ever telling someone they are wrong? Your Christian friend who is sleeping around certainly wants that to be true: live and let live; it’s not your job to tell me, it’s your job to accept and applaud me. The culture has gone so far that anything short of affirmation is called judgment.
excerpts: On one end, judge means to evaluate, discern, or observe: this is good, this is bad, this tastes good, this sounds horrible. Is Jesus forbidding evaluations, criticism, or ever telling someone they are wrong? Your Christian friend who is sleeping around certainly wants that to be true: live and let live; it’s not your job to tell me, it’s your job to accept and applaud me. The culture has gone so far that anything short of affirmation is called judgment.

Jesus can’t mean that, because most of his ministry was telling people they were wrong. In Matthew 22 the Sadducees, who don’t believe in the resurrection, which is why they’re sad, you see, press him, and he says, “You are in error because you do not know the Scriptures or the power of God.” In John 7 he tells his brothers the world hates him because he testifies that its works are evil.
The culture’s view of judgment fails a logic test: aren’t you telling me I’m in error for pointing out errors? You’re doing the thing you tell me not to do.

God gave you grace; shower some of that surplus on them.

Do you remember how hard it was to remove things from your life after Christ? Some are so far removed they’ve forgotten how nasty and dirty they were when he picked them up and dusted them off. Going from pornography to patience and purity, from lust to self-control and faithfulness, from cussing to goodness, from hatred to love, from selfishness to generosity didn’t happen overnight.

Some have been swimming in God’s grace so long they think it’s a private pool party: doing cannonballs while a neighbor shows up bloodied and beaten, looking to wash off, and they worry it will get on them. That is the mindset Jesus rebukes. How you look at others reveals how you think Jesus looks at you; those who find it hard to give grace are the least educated on God’s grace.
Matthew 7 isn’t telling us never to judge anything; it is telling us how. It’s an instruction manual.

“Hey man, I noticed your double take at Miss Tight Dress. Obviously I noticed too. I’ve struggled with my eyes and with lust for years. I’m praying for you; pray for me too. Let’s lock arms, walk face down to the worship center, and sit in the front row so we see nothing but Jesus.” Satan doesn’t know what to do with that. That is love: the error is exposed, and I’m reminded I’m not the only one with a struggle.
It’s all about attitude and approach; that is the difference between biblical and sinful judgment. If their sin stands out more than yours, you’re not ready for surgery; put down the scalpel.

documents.excerpt: It is the final week of the series Courage Over Fear. Joshua is a difficult book that many avoid putting on the teaching calendar, and those who hung in through the whole series know why. excerpts: It is the final week of the series Courage Over Fear. Joshua is a difficult book that many avoid putting on the teaching calendar, and those who hung in through the whole series know why. Josh has learned a lot, and one application keeps hitting over and over: the words Yahweh uses to encourage his young leader Joshua, “Do not be afraid.”

Growing up we feared monsters under the bed, being dumped, not having a prom date, or a bad report card. We don’t grow out of fear; we develop advanced fears. A 2023 survey found 60% of adults feared corruption among government officials, 54% economic collapse, and 52% another world war. We go from monsters under the bed to monsters in government.

God’s word is chock-full of corrupted leaders, governments, and establishments, yet Yahweh’s message to those who love him stays consistent: fear not, take courage, do not lose heart. The command implies a choice: operate in fear or choose to live with courage.

documents.excerpt: After all those external fears, the next thing to torment us is ourselves, especially a fear of our mistakes. Believers grow less fearful of the world and more skeptical of themselves. Living a holy life matters more to us, but that desire can become sinful when we start to fear our own failure and grow apart from grace. Our growing knowledge of righteousness makes our mistakes even more devastating to us.

documents.excerpt: We see it again in the conquest of Canaan. Joshua’s first failure came before the first attack at Ai; his second comes as he handles the Gibeonites in chapter 9. excerpts: We see it again in the conquest of Canaan. Joshua’s first failure came before the first attack at Ai; his second comes as he handles the Gibeonites in chapter 9. excerpts: When you make friends with the enemy, their enemies become your enemies. Adoni-Zedek, king of Jerusalem, heard that Joshua had destroyed Ai and that Gibeon had made peace with Israel, and he was alarmed, because Gibeon was a royal city, larger than Ai, with good fighters.

With a map, Josh shows phase one of the conquest splitting north from south: Jericho, Ai, the trip up to Shechem for worship, and back down through Gilgal, leaving a rectangle of control north of the southern kings. Gibeon is the high ground before upper Beth Horon on a key road to Jerusalem, like hitting the hill before the plateau driving up to Prescott. If you’re a Star Wars fan, you know how important the high ground is: “It’s over, Anakin.” Fun fact: that land later belonged to the tribe of Benjamin; the land divisions are in chapter 13, homework the series won’t cover.

But strategic advantage doesn’t matter when your best warrior is Yahweh. It isn’t about where you fight from but who fights for you; when your best warrior spoke the sun and moon into existence, you don’t need the high ground, though they have it anyway.

documents.excerpt: Josh recently counseled someone troubled that God had gone radio silent, as though they were talking at God rather than with him. He told them: if we aren’t willing to march on what God has already said, why would he speak again? Sometimes you have to call on the promises of old, as Israel did years later in 1 Kings: praise be to the Lord, who has given rest to his people Israel just as he promised; not one word has failed.

documents.context: Josh Wyatt · July 7, 2024 · Courage Over Fear
documents.excerpt: Many believers, to sound super spiritual, have muddied the waters: “The Lord gave me a word for you,” “I had a vision,” “The Lord told me.” Many are always chasing new revelation, and it has gotten so extreme that some churches name their lead pastor and his wife apostles, not the gifting but the office. If he weren’t busy crying, he’d be laughing.
excerpts: Many believers, to sound super spiritual, have muddied the waters: “The Lord gave me a word for you,” “I had a vision,” “The Lord told me.” Many are always chasing new revelation, and it has gotten so extreme that some churches name their lead pastor and his wife apostles, not the gifting but the office. If he weren’t busy crying, he’d be laughing.

Open your Bible: God isn’t dropping new stuff every week; he is dropping the same stuff over and over, probably because we don’t listen. Cessationist, continuationist, or undecided, Josh hopes this body, his responsibility, can agree not to put words in God’s mouth. Instead of asking for a new word, recall the Spirit-inspired Scriptures and ask the Spirit for right understanding, not new understanding. Joseph Smith claimed new revelation; look how that worked out. Ellen White, Mary Baker Eddy, Charles Taze Russell: the list of false teachers is long. Don’t claim words from God; encourage others with the words we know are from God.

documents.excerpt: After an all-night march from Gilgal, Joshua took them by surprise; the Lord threw them into confusion, and Israel defeated them at Gibeon and pursued them toward Beth Horon. Josh read from the NIV, which reads as though the Lord’s only contribution was confusion, but in the original Hebrew the Lord also defeated them, pursued them, and cut them down. He is active in the whole thing.
excerpts: After an all-night march from Gilgal, Joshua took them by surprise; the Lord threw them into confusion, and Israel defeated them at Gibeon and pursued them toward Beth Horon. Josh read from the NIV, which reads as though the Lord’s only contribution was confusion, but in the original Hebrew the Lord also defeated them, pursued them, and cut them down. He is active in the whole thing.

Most of us struggle here because we prefer to shape God into what we want, like pottery growing arms to shape the potter. We like God soft-spoken, distant, around for the holidays, non-combative, affirming. We do the same with Jesus, seeing him less as a warrior for our souls and more as an Old Spice calendar boy with a clean beard and a nice tan. But who is this King of glory? The Lord strong and mighty, mighty in battle. Yahweh is a warrior who crushes the enemy.

documents.excerpt: As the enemy fled toward Azekah, the Lord hurled large hailstones, and more died from the hail than by Israel’s swords. Not only hail on command: this was close sword combat, yet Yahweh threaded the tight spots, hitting the enemy and avoiding friendly fire.
excerpts: As the enemy fled toward Azekah, the Lord hurled large hailstones, and more died from the hail than by Israel’s swords. Not only hail on command: this was close sword combat, yet Yahweh threaded the tight spots, hitting the enemy and avoiding friendly fire.

Josh and his son love a good Nerf battle; his strategy is to hoard the ammo, stashing it in the couch and shutters until everyone wonders where it went. This twisted father’s storehouses are nothing compared to God’s. God puts Job in his place: “Have you entered the storehouses of the snow or seen the storehouses of the hail, which I reserve for times of trouble, for days of war and battle?” God has storehouses full of hail; in 120-degree heat, Josh wants to see the storehouse of snow.

documents.context: Josh Wyatt · July 7, 2024 · Courage Over Fear
documents.excerpt: A quick subject hop, since many ask: should a Christian prepper prepare for terrible times? We can disagree, but Josh’s short answer is yes, as long as it is done in faith, with contingency plans that are courage-driven, not fear-driven. If being prepared means providing for your family and loving your neighbor, share that 25-year-shelf-life Costco food when things go down. But if you have a biometric bunker full of corn, M16s, and landmines, we need to talk.

documents.excerpt: Yahweh’s hailstorm is nothing compared to what comes next. Joshua says before Israel, “Sun, stand still over Gibeon, and you, moon, over the Valley of Aijalon,” and the sun stopped in the middle of the sky about a full day. There has never been a day like it, a day when the Lord listened to a human being. You ask your boss for more time and he adjusts your deadline; Joshua asks God and he adjusts the cosmos.
excerpts: Yahweh’s hailstorm is nothing compared to what comes next. Joshua says before Israel, “Sun, stand still over Gibeon, and you, moon, over the Valley of Aijalon,” and the sun stopped in the middle of the sky about a full day. There has never been a day like it, a day when the Lord listened to a human being. You ask your boss for more time and he adjusts your deadline; Joshua asks God and he adjusts the cosmos.

This is the last and most amazing miracle in Joshua, and many have tried to explain it. Josh decided trying would be a bad idea. Yes, we now know the earth rotates, but we still describe the sun as rising and setting, as Eli pointed out in the teaching team. Wouldn’t stopping the earth cause tsunamis and earthquakes? Josh doesn’t know; maybe God slowed it and brought it back, or bent the light. Just remember he has a storehouse full of snowballs.

documents.excerpt: His ways are above ours, and the secret things belong to him; that’s why it is called a miracle. We can’t explain or comprehend it; the only answer that makes sense is faith: I believe he can, so he did. Seek answers not from people who pretend to have a word from God but from those who actually had one, like Jeremiah: “Ah, Sovereign Lord, you have made the heavens and the earth by your great power and outstretched arm. Nothing is too hard for you.”
excerpts: His ways are above ours, and the secret things belong to him; that’s why it is called a miracle. We can’t explain or comprehend it; the only answer that makes sense is faith: I believe he can, so he did. Seek answers not from people who pretend to have a word from God but from those who actually had one, like Jeremiah: “Ah, Sovereign Lord, you have made the heavens and the earth by your great power and outstretched arm. Nothing is too hard for you.”

Josh finds it hard to believe that in the beginning God made the heavens and the earth and then had no control over them. Psalm 74 says the day and the night are his and he established the sun and moon. Gravity is his design, but he can ignore it if he wants; he is limitless.

Curiosity and questions are fine, but if you don’t believe God is a miracle worker, you must discard the Scriptures, which 2 Timothy says are breathed out by God, then the virgin birth, then the resurrection. You cannot be a Christian and not believe in the miracles of Scripture.
