documents.excerpt: It was a gut punch. One branch has a dad who sexually abused all three of his kids; another has leaf after leaf of alcohol and drug abuse, DWIs, rehab, jail, and arrests. documents.excerpt: Taking the generations back to the beginning, Steve found the human family has always been a train wreck with more twists than a Wetzel’s Pretzel.
excerpts: Taking the generations back to the beginning, Steve found the human family has always been a train wreck with more twists than a Wetzel’s Pretzel.

Earth’s first family: Eve led her husband into disobeying God’s direct command, then their older son killed the younger because he thought God liked him better, and Cain became “the first face on a milk carton.” Noah’s family was saved from global catastrophe, and Noah thanked God by getting drunk and naked; Ham blabbed, Noah cursed him, and “Ham skipped Thanksgiving that year.”

Abraham was called God’s friend and the father of all who believe, but his family was a fiasco too: when Sarah couldn’t conceive, Abraham slept with a slave girl at Sarah’s suggestion, and then Sarah kicked Hagar and Ishmael off the family plantation. Barely out of the gate, the human genogram includes murder, infidelity, drunkenness, half brothers, mistresses, neglect, and abuse, and Ishmael’s legacy of anger is why the Middle East is on fire today.

When Jacob admits the plan is sketchy, he isn’t repenting, just confessing. He is still going to do it; he is only worried about the repercussions. Confessing a sin you still plan to do just says, “I hope I don’t get caught.” Repentance admits what I want to do is wrong, so I stop, drop, and stroll the other direction, living for the Lord instead of my own desires.
Jacob’s solution was to be sneakier: “Is there anything we can do to sin better?” Mama said, “Let the curse fall on me. Just do as I say.” Don’t bother with what God has said.

documents.excerpt: We try to compartmentalize Jesus’ lordship: as long as I declare it with my mouth, it’s all good, even with slippage in how I practice it with the rest of my body. But if Jesus is to have supremacy in all things, and he isn’t Lord of all, he isn’t Lord at all.
excerpts: We try to compartmentalize Jesus’ lordship: as long as I declare it with my mouth, it’s all good, even with slippage in how I practice it with the rest of my body. But if Jesus is to have supremacy in all things, and he isn’t Lord of all, he isn’t Lord at all.

“Most everything else is in alignment, just this one little exception”: too much alcohol, certain chemicals, an affair, porn, flirting at the bar, lying to my wife and ignoring my kids. Compartmentalizing leads to duplicity, a distracted, divided mind, and Jesus said nobody can serve two masters. A divided life always seeps, and once a leak begins it is hard to get it back in the bottle. Making Jesus Lord of some parts but not all is dangerous and never works.

documents.excerpt: As the church bows and prepares for the Lord’s Supper, Steve asks the burning question: Where am I stopping short? It is in the small things we think aren’t a big deal, exactly what Jacob thought, and he had no idea what his decisions would cost him and others.
excerpts: As the church bows and prepares for the Lord’s Supper, Steve asks the burning question: Where am I stopping short? It is in the small things we think aren’t a big deal, exactly what Jacob thought, and he had no idea what his decisions would cost him and others.

Steve believes the time is short and the coming of our Lord is at hand. The world is at a tipping point, and while he has no inside information, he believes it because Jesus said it, and the righteous judge is standing at the door. Wouldn’t you rather Jesus find you right in the center of his will than living just 20 miles short of where he wants you to be?

Genesis 22 and the covenant promise
As the series in Genesis continues, the church lands in chapter 22. Genesis has two major themes: chapters 1 to 11 are about creation, and chapters 12 to 50 are about the covenant.
In chapter 12 the Lord promises Abram a great nation, a great name, and blessing: “God’s like, I got your back.” In chapter 15 comes the promise of a son from his own body. In chapter 21 Sarah becomes pregnant and bears a son in Abraham’s old age, at the very time God had promised.
Josh asks the church to imagine the joy Abraham and Sarah must have felt: finally, their miracle son, the first baby under the promise, the first star.
documents.title: Genesis 22 and the covenant promise — Here I Am!

excerpts: God won’t test a baby believer the way he tests a mature believer. If you are on a milk diet, the Lord isn’t having you bench press to failure. God grows our faith through testing, and the trials don’t get easier; expect them to become exceedingly great as you look more like Jesus. Don’t mistake following Jesus for a smooth, paved path to heaven.

Our country’s most elite soldiers, Navy SEALs, Delta Force, Army Rangers, go on the hardest missions. BUD/S, the Navy SEAL training ground, is a 24-week course with a dropout rate around 80 percent; many dream of being elite, but few endure the test.

Why would God grow you as a soldier for Jesus only to send you on the same missions he sent you on as a grunt? The more you look like Christ, the bigger the storm you can endure and the greater the missions he sends you on.

documents.excerpt: God said, “Take your son, your only son, whom you love.” Josh comes from a long line of only sons: his dad, himself, and his son. With two sons he would love them both, but there is something to be said about there being only one.
excerpts: God said, “Take your son, your only son, whom you love.” Josh comes from a long line of only sons: his dad, himself, and his son. With two sons he would love them both, but there is something to be said about there being only one.

God has watched Abraham with Isaac and knows how much he loves that boy. Unlike many fathers today who think fatherhood ends with getting a woman pregnant, Abraham knows showing up matters, and he takes seriously his job to shape Isaac into a man of faith.

Some say Isaac was between 15 and 35; some commentators say a teenage boy, and Josephus says he was in his 30s. We don’t really know, but Abraham was 100 when this miracle baby was born. He tucked him in, taught him to hunt, fish, and pray; they counted the stars and remembered God’s promises together, a bond so deep only death could break it.

“Here I am, Lord. What’s next?”
Every step of the way God said go and Abraham obeyed. Then God calls and Abraham answers, eager: “What’s next? I can’t wait to see what you have for us.” And God says, “Go kill your son. No, not that one. That one.” How is he going to explain this to Sarah?

Jesus is “God in a flesh suit.” He lived the perfect life and died on the cross to pay the penalty for our sins, the death we should have died. We all deserve hell, separated from God by nature and by choice; either we die for our sins or Jesus dies as our substitute.

documents.excerpt: We continue in Genesis 19, one of the most difficult, controversial, and important sections in the entire Bible. Josh jokes that he won’t be shaking many hands in the lobby after this one.
excerpts: We continue in Genesis 19, one of the most difficult, controversial, and important sections in the entire Bible. Josh jokes that he won’t be shaking many hands in the lobby after this one.

His motivation is to explain the text in a way that helps people better understand God and the magnitude of their sin. He isn’t trying to beat anyone over the head or take the moral high ground; he isn’t against them or the people they love. He is against Satan convincing people it is okay to stay in their sin.

Plenty of people will affirm you, tell you you’re perfect just the way you are, and say nothing bad will come of a lifestyle of sin, claiming they love you because they accept you no matter what. They don’t love you; they love themselves, which is why they would never sacrifice their reputation to tell you the truth. Josh loves people enough to tell the truth, knowing some may leave and tell their neighbors the pastor is a bigot and a hater.

Who loves people more: the one who pleads with them to leave a wicked lifestyle, or the one who says the Bible is just an ancient text that doesn’t mean what it says, so go ahead? Who loves sinners more, the one who preaches acceptance or the one who preaches repentance? Isaiah 5 says woe to those who call evil good.

People no longer feel guilty when they turn from what was once considered right; the moral code is being hijacked and is based on how you feel in the moment, not on what God says. We do the same with God: instead of seeing his justice as evidence of his love, many claim it proves he is unloving. We have taken the author of all that is good and labeled him evil because he says no to bad things.

If after today you want to leave a life of sin but don’t know how, or your sin is tied to your career and you can’t see how to make it work, Josh doesn’t know how either, but this church body will commit to serve and support you through that transition. Our hearts are filled not with condemnation but with compassion.

documents.excerpt: Before the details of Genesis 19, Josh wants people to see where it fits in our understanding of God and his plan to reconcile sinners to himself. There is no separation from Genesis to Jesus. A Mary Poppins view of Jesus, a nice nanny with an umbrella, isn’t accurate. Jesus is King of kings and Lord of lords. He traded equality with God, became a man, was marginalized, mocked, and spit upon, and came not to be served but to serve and give his life as a ransom for many.
excerpts: Before the details of Genesis 19, Josh wants people to see where it fits in our understanding of God and his plan to reconcile sinners to himself. There is no separation from Genesis to Jesus. A Mary Poppins view of Jesus, a nice nanny with an umbrella, isn’t accurate. Jesus is King of kings and Lord of lords. He traded equality with God, became a man, was marginalized, mocked, and spit upon, and came not to be served but to serve and give his life as a ransom for many.

Christians get excited about that, and the world has no problem with a gentle Jesus, the sacrificial lamb. Things take on another tone when we talk about Jesus returning with a sword, rewarding what you’ve done, judging what is done in secret, separating good and evil, and establishing a perfect kingdom. It is nice to hear Jesus died for our sins, to which our culture says, “Well, I’m worth dying for.”

We love hearing about grace, but listen to Jude: certain individuals whose condemnation was written about long ago have secretly slipped in among you, ungodly people who pervert the grace of God into a license for immorality and deny Jesus Christ our only Sovereign and Lord. This is happening. Paul would say, “Shall we go on sinning so that grace may increase? Certainly not.” Christ’s victory over sin and death isn’t a hall pass to sin. Your sin matters, how you deal with it matters, and how you deal with others’ sin matters.

documents.excerpt: There is archaeological evidence for this. Joel Kramer, a Christian archaeologist on YouTube, shows a layer of ash with burnt pottery and heat-stained human remains, bones warped and bent by intense heat, and sulfur balls he pulls from the ground that are still flammable. What about your daughters, fool? Aren’t they under the protection of your roof? Josh would die a thousand deaths before handing his daughter over to be raped by a mob, and he would take some with him.

excerpts: Lot doesn’t cry out to God for help, doesn’t pray, and doesn’t seek counsel from the wisdom in his own house. He waited to act and is backed into a corner. But the men inside pulled Lot back into the house, shut the door, and struck the men at the door, young and old, with blindness: a riot of biblical proportion, blind punches thrown everywhere.

The two men said, “Do you have anyone else here, sons-in-law, sons or daughters, or anyone else in the city who belongs to you? Get them out of here, because we are going to destroy this place.” Grab your kids, your family, your wife; we’ve seen enough.

Lot spoke to his sons-in-law, pledged to marry his daughters. Imagine that conversation: “You did what?” This can happen to anyone; a believer can surround himself with the wrong people and become a twisted mess of faith and funk. “Hurry and get out; the Lord is about to destroy the city.” But his sons-in-law thought he was joking.

How you lead your family now will most definitely affect how they treat you later. It is an extreme example, but presenting your daughters to be raped by a mob will leave lasting scars. They watched their dad operate for years, so it shouldn’t surprise us when, a few verses later, they get him drunk and have sex with him to preserve the family line.

documents.context: Josh Wyatt · February 4, 2024 · Genesis
documents.excerpt: With the coming of dawn the angels urged Lot to hurry and take his wife and two daughters or be swept away. When he hesitated, the men grasped his hand and the hands of his wife and daughters and led them safely out of the city, for the Lord was merciful to them.
excerpts: With the coming of dawn the angels urged Lot to hurry and take his wife and two daughters or be swept away. When he hesitated, the men grasped his hand and the hands of his wife and daughters and led them safely out of the city, for the Lord was merciful to them.
Why did Lot hesitate? Josh doesn’t think he was submitting a prayer request on the church app. He thinks Lot was dreading life outside the walls.

Here we get frustrated with Lot, the one we were cheering: “You coward, you punk.” But are you really that different? God floods your life with mercy and says, “I’ve forgiven you; leave your life of sin,” and you say, “Check in with me in a month. Is it really a sin? It’s not hurting anyone. Can’t I follow Jesus and keep doing this?” None of us is better than Lot. We hesitate too, clinging to our sin while claiming to follow the one who died to overcome it.

Yet notice the Lord’s mercy: “Okay, Lot, you don’t want to lead your family right now; you’re sad to leave that life. I’ll make sure they’re with us.” Isn’t it amazing how far you can fall and still be considered worth saving? We want to condemn and disqualify Lot, but the Lord keeps dragging them out.

documents.excerpt: As soon as they were out, one of them said, “Flee for your lives! Don’t look back, and don’t stop anywhere in the plain! Flee to the mountains or you will be swept away!” People ask Josh how to leave their sin life; Genesis 19:17 explains how believers deal with sin: flee, don’t look back, don’t stop. Kill it before it kills you.
excerpts: As soon as they were out, one of them said, “Flee for your lives! Don’t look back, and don’t stop anywhere in the plain! Flee to the mountains or you will be swept away!” People ask Josh how to leave their sin life; Genesis 19:17 explains how believers deal with sin: flee, don’t look back, don’t stop. Kill it before it kills you.

Many of us say, “Is this really a big deal? It’s just a little pot; I can stop looking at porn anytime; I’ll stop drinking in a couple of months, plus the holidays are coming.” No: run, stop thinking about it, and go. Don’t regret dropping that filthy habit for Jesus.

Jesus talks about looking back when invited forward. He says, “Follow me,” and someone answers, “I will follow you, but first let me go back and say goodbye to my family.” Jesus replied, “No one who puts a hand to the plow and looks back is fit for service in the kingdom of God.” Followers of Christ have eyes up, moving forward; we operate not on our past but on what he says about our future.

But Lot’s wife looked back, and she became a pillar of salt. Once you have Jesus, there is no reason to look back. Believers, flee this corrupt world. Your response to Sodom and Gomorrah should be to run to Jesus: we are wicked and he is good, so grab his hand, run from your sin together, and never look back. Do not conform to the pattern of this world, but be transformed by the renewing of your mind.

To evangelists: you won’t win anyone for Christ if you look nothing like Christ. He has shown you what is good and what the Lord requires: to act justly, to love mercy, and to walk humbly with your God. You know what is keeping you from walking like that and from Jesus. If you need help, ask God; he is alive, active, and powerful, and he will reach into your life and help you. Call out to him.

documents.excerpt: Paul gives a clear order of operation for God’s plan of redemption in Romans 8: those God foreknew he also predestined to be conformed to the image of his Son, and those he predestined he called, those he called he justified, and those he justified he glorified.
excerpts: Paul gives a clear order of operation for God’s plan of redemption in Romans 8: those God foreknew he also predestined to be conformed to the image of his Son, and those he predestined he called, those he called he justified, and those he justified he glorified.

That is one reason there is no such thing as an arrogant Christian: you didn’t choose God; he chose you. Josh wholeheartedly believes Scripture teaches that a person genuinely saved is eternally saved; you can never be snatched out or lose the new life God gave you through Jesus Christ. Paul preached this everywhere; to the Romans he says that in all things God works for the good of those who love him, who have been called according to his purpose.

Ladies, your husband might have unfinished projects all over the house, but God doesn’t leave things unfinished. Abel, Enoch, Noah, Abraham, Sarah, Isaac, Jacob, Joseph, Moses, Joshua, Rahab, Gideon, Barak, Samson, Jephthah, David, Samuel, Mary, Joseph, John: like the Hebrew writer, Josh doesn’t have time to list all who walked by faith. They were certain of what they did not see and confident that he who began a good work in them would carry it on to completion until the day of Christ Jesus.
Abraham paved the way by living utterly convinced God would do exactly what he said. He knew that those God calls he also justifies, and those he justifies he also glorifies.

documents.excerpt: Josh and his wife don’t tolerate kids talking back. When a command has been spoken in the house and the kids come back with questions, he says, “Just drop them in the suggestion box, kiddo.” “But Dad, there is no suggestion box.” “Exactly. excerpts: Josh and his wife don’t tolerate kids talking back. When a command has been spoken in the house and the kids come back with questions, he says, “Just drop them in the suggestion box, kiddo.” “But Dad, there is no suggestion box.” “Exactly. Now go do what I asked.” Great news: God is a way better father than Josh is.

The church seems to treat doubt like an infectious disease, as if getting too close might rub off on you: contagious cooties. But there is a big difference between doubt and unbelief. Josh doesn’t think doubt disrupts faith; it has the potential to develop faith: “God, I believe you are the one true God, that you are good and working for my good, but I can’t see it right now. You said you’d do this and I believe you will, but it isn’t happening, and I’m bringing it to you because I’m frustrated, or I’m afraid.”

Doubt wants to see God; unbelief wants to dismiss God. Unbelief walks away saying, “God, you’re not good, and you won’t do what you said.” Doubt assumes God will do it but hasn’t yet; unbelief assumes God is a liar and never will. Big difference.

documents.excerpt: God tells Abram, “I’m your very great reward,” and in a beautiful moment Abram shares his doubts in verse 2: “Sovereign Lord, what can you give me since I remain childless and the one who will inherit my estate is Eliezer of Damascus? You have given me no children, so a servant in my household will be my heir.” How can God make him a nation without an heir? How can he know God will actually do what he said?
excerpts: God tells Abram, “I’m your very great reward,” and in a beautiful moment Abram shares his doubts in verse 2: “Sovereign Lord, what can you give me since I remain childless and the one who will inherit my estate is Eliezer of Damascus? You have given me no children, so a servant in my household will be my heir.” How can God make him a nation without an heir? How can he know God will actually do what he said?

Then the word of the Lord came: “This man will not be your heir, but a son coming from your own body.” He took him outside: “Look up at the heavens and count the stars, if indeed you can count them. So shall your offspring be.” One, two... not literally; it is an illustration.

In effect God says: look at the stars; that is how many people depend on my promise. I’m never going to let you down, and do you honestly think I’ll fail all of them? My promises are about the entire world, people from every nation and tongue. I’m working my redemption plan for all of them, preparing a way for Jesus, building a highway for the Messiah. Every star needs a Savior, a shield, a new heart and a new life; that is how many people I love and am sending my Son to die for. Every star has a name, and I know how many hairs are on every head. Don’t be afraid. I said I’d do it. I will.

excerpts: What is your response? Abram responded in verse 6: Abram believed the Lord, and he credited it to him as righteousness. The word of the Lord came to Abram, and Abram believed the Lord. This is how it will always work: God speaks, we believe; God promises, we trust.

Josh doesn’t know everyone’s name or what they came in with, but he has to ask: if you die tonight, do you know where you will spend eternity? He is certain he is spending eternity in heaven with the Lord. Are you?

He knows his future not because he is clairvoyant or knows something special, but because God spoke it and he believes him. The Word became flesh, and Josh took God at his word. Who is your authority on matters of eternal life and death? Who do you trust and listen to? Abram believed the word of the Lord, and that is why Christians carry the Bible like a gun and cling to it: it is the word of God.

excerpts: As God came to Abram in a vision, he has come to us through his word, and from Genesis to Revelation it is about Jesus Christ. Jesus came because you needed something other than your own righteousness. You can’t do it, and he knew you couldn’t, so he did it for you.

When we present the best possible versions of ourselves, it is nothing but filthy rags. God isn’t impressed. As last week showed, the intentions of your heart are only evil all the time; he knows your heart, motives, and actions. “Fine, God, how do we fix this? What do I need to do?” Nothing. It is about what he does for you: “I’ll do this for you. Just trust me,” just as he told Abram.

Because of his great love for us, God, who is rich in mercy, made us alive with Christ even when we were dead in transgressions; it is by grace you have been saved. Josh was dead and now is alive. Jesus died to save him, and God raised him three days later, so the one who died to save him is still alive. Hallelujah.

Just as people are destined to die once and after that face judgment, so Christ was sacrificed once to take away the sins of many, and he will appear a second time, not to bear sin, but to bring salvation to those waiting for him. Josh is waiting for him and hanging on his every word.

excerpts: God keeps addressing the doubt with something special in verse 9. If God assures those he loves by making promises, we should assure those we love by reminding them of his promises.

The Lord said, “Bring me a heifer, a goat and a ram, each three years old, along with a dove and a young pigeon.” Abram, who will ask God anything, doesn’t ask a single question; God gives no instruction, yet Abram knows what to do, so it was probably familiar to him. He cut them in two and arranged the halves opposite each other, but not the birds. Josh’s wife, their little Snow White who loves birds, is probably sighing with relief; Leviticus 1 says we aren’t supposed to separate birds in half. A big win for bird lovers.

Why the sacrifices and the cutting? They are about to make a covenant, a contract; it literally means the cutting of a covenant. Today we use DocuSign: write down the agreement, both sign on the dotted line, and if you break your word I can sue you for breach of contract. That is how a written culture does it, but in an oral culture like Abram’s, they acted it out. The creative arts people want to act it out; no, we can’t.

They acted out the consequences of breaking your word (if discipline isn’t working at home, you could try this; just saying). In Jeremiah the Lord says that those who violated his covenant, the leaders, officials, priests, and people who walked between the pieces of the calf they cut in two, he will hand over to their enemies, and their dead bodies will become food for the birds and wild animals.

So you cut the animals in half, walked between the pieces, and said, “If I don’t keep my word, may I be as these animals; may I be cut to pieces and my body be food for the birds.” It was intense, and people kept their word, unlike today: “I wasn’t in my proper mind when I signed that; I think that says Daffy Duck.”

So you cut the animals in half, walked between the pieces, and said, “If I don’t keep my word, may I be as these animals; may I be cut to pieces and my body be food for the birds.” It was intense, and people kept their word, unlike today: “I wasn’t in my proper mind when I signed that; I think that says Daffy Duck.”

excerpts: Abram thinks he is about to walk through the pieces, a big moment of spoken promises between him and God. Instead something even more amazing happens: as the sun was setting, Abram fell into a deep sleep, and a thick and dreadful darkness came over him.

Recap why: Abram had doubts because he didn’t have a son yet. So God, the sovereign one, is about to reveal the future: “Let me show you.” Be careful what you ask for. “Know for certain that for 400 years your descendants will be strangers in a country not their own, enslaved and mistreated, but I will punish the nation they serve, and they will come out with great possessions. You will go to your ancestors in peace at a good old age. In the fourth generation your descendants will come back, for the sin of the Amorites has not yet reached its full measure.”

Josh doesn’t want to know the future even if he could; it comes with baggage he doesn’t want, and God’s ways are above his. God tells Abram there will be tough years ahead, because he will be patient with the Amorites, still offering them the opportunity to repent even though he knows they won’t, and Abram’s descendants will endure those years as he displays his divine patience for generations.

A shield not only protects you from getting hurt; it also keeps your eyes from seeing hard things on the other side you might not understand. Did they get the land after the Exodus? No, not until Joshua. Abram is struggling with not having a son, and God is working a plan that stretches over generations.

We get impatient too. We want to see the day of the Lord, and there is nothing wrong with that hope: maranatha, come Lord Jesus. But God says, in effect, “I know you are looking forward to paradise, no more pain, tears, or sadness, but I want to save more people. I was patient and kind with you; I’m going to be patient and kind with the Amorites too. I’m the same God, there is more going on than you can see. Do you trust me?”

The words for smoking firepot and blazing torch are also used when God descends on Mount Sinai; they are words used when God shows up physically. This is a big moment.

“Blazing torch” is often used for lightning. We are used to lightning flashing and then gone; this is blazing lightning. Imagine the crackling sound, the sparks, the heat, as it passes between the pieces.

God is signing on the dotted line, walking between the pieces and saying, “If I don’t do what I told you I’d do, may I be like these pieces.” He doesn’t say, “Abram, you go first; show me you’re all in, then I’ll commit to you.” He says, “I commit myself to you. Period. Got a pen? No? It’s okay, I’ll use lightning.”

documents.excerpt: Jesus made promises too. If you are struggling or doubting, become a scholar of Christ’s promises: know them, memorize them, remember them, recall them.
excerpts: Jesus made promises too. If you are struggling or doubting, become a scholar of Christ’s promises: know them, memorize them, remember them, recall them.

John 6: all whom the Father gives me will come to me, and whoever comes to me I will never drive away. Those who are his are his forever. Matthew 4: follow me, and I will make you fishers of men. Jesus promises not only life after death but a life of purpose now; you may feel inadequate and afraid like Abram, but Jesus will lead your transformation if you follow him.
Matthew 11: come to me, all you who are weary and burdened, and I will give you rest. Salvation is a gift; you don’t deserve it or earn it; Jesus did it for you, so rest in him.

Jesus promises the Holy Spirit: “I will ask the Father, and he will give you another advocate to help you and be with you forever, the Spirit of truth.” The world can’t accept him, but you know him, for he lives with you and will be in you. Jesus later explains that the Comforter will convict the world of sin, righteousness, and judgment, so he will guide us as we walk in new life.

And look at this promise: “My Father’s house has plenty of room; if that were not so, would I have told you that I am going there to prepare a place for you? And if I go and prepare a place for you, I will come back and take you to be with me.” I will come back.

documents.context: Josh Wyatt · January 28, 2024 · Genesis
documents.excerpt: Josh hopes people respond to Jesus today: by singing, giving a tithe, or taking communion. Two chalkboards, front and back, are for shouting your doubt: make known, as Abram did, what you are wrestling with and your frustrations, doubts about God and what he is doing, or about yourself. You don’t grow in faith by burying it or pretending it isn’t there, but by trusting God to work through it.
excerpts: Josh hopes people respond to Jesus today: by singing, giving a tithe, or taking communion. Two chalkboards, front and back, are for shouting your doubt: make known, as Abram did, what you are wrestling with and your frustrations, doubts about God and what he is doing, or about yourself. You don’t grow in faith by burying it or pretending it isn’t there, but by trusting God to work through it.

He hasn’t lived that long, but he knows life is so much better when you surrender. Stop fighting a fight that is already over. Write it down, then pray with the person next to you a simple prayer: “Lord, fill us with reminders of your promises.” Leave the thing that frustrates your faith behind; the enemy loves the shadows, so drag your fears, burdens, anxieties, frustrations, and doubts into the light.

Then go to the Lord’s table, look at the board, and remember the sacrifice of Jesus: his body and blood remind us God was willing to send his only Son to die on a cross so his covenant of love would be available to everyone who believes.

If you decide to follow Jesus, the waters of baptism are ready; you don’t need a T-shirt. The Christian walk isn’t private; secret Christians are counterfeit Christians, and real faith can’t be kept to yourself. Repent and ask God to forgive you; he is faithful and just and will forgive your sins and cleanse you from all unrighteousness. Baptism is a public sign of what is happening in your heart. Don’t wait; tell the world what the Lord has done for you.

documents.excerpt: We pick up in Genesis 5. Josh loves looking at the life of Noah, but it blows his mind that this story has been such a success with children. He gets the animals holding hands, or hooves, as they enter the ark two by two, but literally the entire planet dies.
excerpts: We pick up in Genesis 5. Josh loves looking at the life of Noah, but it blows his mind that this story has been such a success with children. He gets the animals holding hands, or hooves, as they enter the ark two by two, but literally the entire planet dies.

This isn’t a cute story; it is a terrifying story about God’s righteous judgment: massive destruction, dead bodies floating around, and Noah’s family stuck in a boat with all those animals for months with no arrival time. Some couldn’t even drive to church without arguing with their family. “Are we there yet?” “No, Shem, and if you ask one more time I’m going to pull this boat over.”

Joking aside, these chapters teach us about humanity and our wickedness, and about God’s response to wickedness: his patience, love, mercy, goodness, and compassion. Josh’s prayer through this series is that people would see the goodness of Jesus. The most terrifying moments in history aren’t that terrifying if you have found peace with God through Jesus Christ.

documents.excerpt: All the days of Enoch were 365 years. Enoch walked with God, and he was not, for God took him. That’s different. Everyone else has babies in retirement and lives another 800 years, but not Enoch: Enoch walks with God.
excerpts: All the days of Enoch were 365 years. Enoch walked with God, and he was not, for God took him. That’s different. Everyone else has babies in retirement and lives another 800 years, but not Enoch: Enoch walks with God.

Watch closely or you’ll miss Enoch’s importance. Everyone wants to talk about God’s judgment, and in Genesis it is hard to miss, but it isn’t just death and destruction. Notice where there is life: there is life when anyone walks with God. Adam and Eve walked with God in the cool of the day; Enoch, Noah, Abraham, David, Isaiah, John, and Paul walked with God. None were perfect, but they walked with God. Do you?

We are all born into this fallen world. Romans 3:23: for all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God. Romans 6:23: for the wages of sin is death. We will all live however many years we live and then die, vegan, fish oil, only carrots, it doesn’t matter. Aren’t you glad you came to church this morning?

If you want to conquer death, it isn’t about diet, exercise, supplements, genetics, or choosing not to skydive. The only way to conquer death is to walk with God. Do you know him, spend time with him, consider him day in and day out? Most people know how to make a child; it is another thing entirely to raise one. Checking boxes is one thing; walking with God, letting him lead you and praying for him to change you, is another.

documents.excerpt: To answer whether you are walking faithfully like Enoch, check yourself against the church’s core values. Anyone can line up with them temporarily; the question is whether you desire these things more and more.
excerpts: To answer whether you are walking faithfully like Enoch, check yourself against the church’s core values. Anyone can line up with them temporarily; the question is whether you desire these things more and more.

Be doers: do you have a growing hunger and thirst not just to know his word but to be moved by it and obey it, even if you have to shred some things in your life? Be humble: do you walk around like your stuff doesn’t stink, flexing YouTube knowledge in lobby debates that you aren’t putting into practice, or are you washing feet and serving others?

Sing praise: are you anxious to worship him, or looking for ways to avoid it? Josh felt out of whack after missing last week’s corporate worship; he had been worshiping all week, but he missed their voices and the beauty of the saints singing together.

Show love, forgive freely, serve others, pray always: is your church family life radiating with these? To be honest, if you can leave the church you call home and not even say bye, it wasn’t home and you weren’t doing church. Are you praying with, forgiving, and serving your brothers and sisters? That is what Enoch’s life looks like.

Give generously: are you tithing? Have you ever looked at your paycheck and said, “God, you’re first. You gave me these abilities and opportunities. Take it, multiply it, grow your kingdom; if you bless me, I’ll become more generous, because that’s what you did for me. My wallet isn’t off limits to you”? God doesn’t ask for everything, just a slice. How much do you invest in your kingdom, and how much in his?
Suffer well: when hard times come, do you look up and praise him or shake your fist? How we suffer is our testimony to God’s goodness.

excerpts: At the back end of the genealogy, all the days of Methuselah were 969 years, and he died: the oldest man in the Bible. Enoch lived 365 years; Methuselah lived 969. Church quiz: who lived the better life?
Everyone seems to think the key to a great life is longevity, and there is nothing wrong with a long life, but there is more to it. Josh would rather have 20 years with God than 80 without him.

He has seen it play out at baptisms. There is never anything sad about someone being baptized into Christ, but older folks sometimes come out of the water and have to deal with a little shame and sadness, feeling they missed a whole life they could have spent walking with the Lord. There is more value in one year walking with the Lord than a hundred without him. It isn’t just how long or how well you live, but who you live for.

excerpts: God’s response may sound odd if you see him as far off, impersonal, and unrelatable. He isn’t far off; the incarnation of Christ shows he is with us and among us. And God has emotions like you and me, except that he has a handle on them: his anger is righteous, his jealousy is right, his justice is right, his love is unconditional.

The Lord regretted that he had made man on the earth, and it grieved him to his heart. “Grieved” is the same word Isaiah uses for how an abandoned wife feels. Many know that rejection, and some are in it now. God isn’t some impersonal being on cosmic overwatch; he knows rejection too. He has felt it, endured it, and been patient through it. Don’t give up: the flood waters and the winds obey him, and he will bring you back because he said he would.

Some say God’s regret means he changed his mind, but those who know the Lord know he doesn’t change; through Malachi he says, “For I the Lord do not change.” If God regretted us to the point of not wanting humanity to exist, why have Noah build the ark at all? His regret is his pain and sorrow; as Jesus wept over Jerusalem, God wept over the condition of humanity.

Many picture God as an irrational dictator instead of the patient father he is. In nearly 1,700 years of history, one man is mentioned as walking faithfully with God while generations dove headfirst into corruption and scandal, and nobody else seemed to care.

People object, “That’s not fair,” but you only think it unfair if you are a sinner, because sinners don’t like justice unless it is for somebody else. If someone intended only evil toward you all the time and wouldn’t stop unless wiped out, you would want justice. But if you were the wicked one, would you want justice or mercy? We scream for justice until it is aimed at us. God seeks justice even when it is aimed at his Son. There is only one who is good.

documents.excerpt: But God also responds with mercy. Meet Noah. Spoiler alert: he is going to build a big boat, and God will spare him and his family; Peter tells us eight souls received God’s mercy.
excerpts: But God also responds with mercy. Meet Noah. Spoiler alert: he is going to build a big boat, and God will spare him and his family; Peter tells us eight souls received God’s mercy.

Why Noah? Some go to the next verse: he walked with God, he was blameless, he was righteous. But if you have been told God chose Noah as a standout candidate with a spotless resume, you got bad information. There was nothing special about Noah. The idea that God loves good people and hates bad people, so the good get on the boat and the bad had better swim, isn’t taught anywhere in Scripture. There are no good people, just bad people; God was grieved over all of mankind, including Noah.

Don’t miss the order of operation: Noah found favor, grace, in the eyes of the Lord. Noah was righteous and faithful because of God’s grace; God’s grace wasn’t a result of Noah’s righteousness. It is the first time we see the Hebrew word for grace in the Bible, hen. Noah wasn’t special; he heard God’s voice and responded.

Hebrews 13 says Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever. Nothing has changed: we are saved by grace. You don’t deserve it or earn it, so there is no glory, boasting, pride, trophy, or credit for you. We boast in the cross, in being loved, in his grace. Josh was wicked, God changed him and is still changing him, and the only explanation he has is God.

documents.excerpt: Imagine Josh’s surprise that after receiving salvation God keeps hitting him with blessings. For most of his life his relationships were a mess, one toxic relationship after another, and even how he met his wife might make some cringe. Then God went to work on them.
excerpts: Imagine Josh’s surprise that after receiving salvation God keeps hitting him with blessings. For most of his life his relationships were a mess, one toxic relationship after another, and even how he met his wife might make some cringe. Then God went to work on them.

He wakes up next to the most beautiful woman in the world, who was somehow convinced by God that he was husband material: grace. Two children who love Jesus: grace. He and his wife have been sad, rejoiced, buried loved ones, lost, and won together: grace. From toxic relationships to a God-honoring marriage, from hating the church to leading her, walking away from addictions even after going into ministry: grace upon grace upon grace.

It all started when Jesus said, “Trust me, Josh. I took your sin so you can take my righteousness. I want to walk with you, love you, be your Savior and Lord. I’m going to do all the work, and you’re going to be a co-heir with me.” “Okay, Jesus, I’m down.”

To those screaming that God is unfair: isn’t that completely unfair? Christ died for our sins, conquered sin and death, and will reign forever, and Josh gets to reign with him, though he is one of the reasons Jesus endured the cross. Yet he is more than a conqueror through him who loved him.
You don’t clean up your life hoping God will love you; you clean it up in response to his love.

Part of being faithful is saying yes to the task even when you can’t see how it is possible: “God, I’ll do whatever you say, go wherever you lead, say whatever you want. I’d rather fail with you than succeed without you.”

Noah did all that the Lord commanded, and nothing has changed in how we follow Christ: God commands, Noah obeys; Christ teaches, we obey. Jesus told his disciples, “If you love me, you’ll keep my commands.” Noah loved the Lord.

That hasn’t changed: 1 John 4, we love because he first loved us.

excerpts: Josh pleads: don’t let the door shut before you decide to give your life to Christ. Stop waiting. Jesus promised he would come again and connected it to Noah: as it was in the days of Noah, so it will be at the coming of the Son of Man. The Lord was grieved because his creation rejected him and kept living as they pleased; they did it then and are doing it now, and just as the flood came out of nowhere, so will the sword.

The first judgment was by water, and that will never happen again; God’s covenant with Noah is set in the sky, and you might even see it today. He promised. Speaking of wickedness, our culture has taken the symbol of that promise and made it a symbol of pride to boast in sexual immorality.

They mock: “Where is he? He said he was coming back. Where’s your Jesus now?” Believers know he isn’t slow and hasn’t forgotten; he is patient, giving every possible opportunity to trust him. He doesn’t want anyone to perish; he wants us saved by his wonderful grace, receiving a righteousness not our own through faith in Christ. He waits because the second judgment will be by fire.
Come to Jesus. No one knows the day or the hour the door will shut, but when it does, we would rather you be on the inside. Believe, be baptized, and be saved.

documents.excerpt: Few chapters in the Bible are more widely mocked than Genesis 3: a talking snake, an angel wielding a lightsaber, an apple dangling from a tree, and a naked man and woman with her long flowing hair covering all the necessary bits. Steve gets it; the whole scene is viewed as kind of a joke.
excerpts: Few chapters in the Bible are more widely mocked than Genesis 3: a talking snake, an angel wielding a lightsaber, an apple dangling from a tree, and a naked man and woman with her long flowing hair covering all the necessary bits. Steve gets it; the whole scene is viewed as kind of a joke.

Yet what gets unpacked is the most consequential event in human history. Never mind 9/11 or October 7; set aside Hitler, Pearl Harbor, even the Holocaust. Genesis 3 surpasses even the invention of electricity and the internet, with apologies to Al Gore.
What happened in Genesis 3 changed everything. It is no exaggeration to say that you and I now live in a post Genesis 3 world. Everything you see and experience is not at all the utopia God intended.

excerpts: The world as it is isn’t the world as it once was in Genesis 1, when God reviewed his handiwork, saw all that he had made, and it was very good. The whole world moved in a perfect, God-paced rhythm. God was so impressed by his handiwork that he tells the creation story again in chapter 2 with more detail.

Adam and Eve lived in a perfect world, in a state of innocence, totally free from sin: no anger, no hostility, just two naked people, beautiful and unashamed, living an old-fashioned love song coming down in two-part harmony. That one is for the old people.

All that glorious harmony lasted 7.2 seconds. All it took was the turn of a page. In Genesis 3 everything goes bad, fatally, terminally, generationally bad, and every human since, everyone living in this post Genesis 3 world, lives with the dreadful aftereffects.

documents.excerpt: To understand how Genesis 3 even happened, we have to go back before the beginning. Before the beginning there was a great conflict in heaven: a deity denier disputed God’s right to sit on the throne, and a battle ensued between God and this adversary. He goes by many names: Beelzebub, devil, dragon, the evil one, the god of this age, Leviathan, roaring lion, Satan, serpent, thief, and more.
excerpts: To understand how Genesis 3 even happened, we have to go back before the beginning. Before the beginning there was a great conflict in heaven: a deity denier disputed God’s right to sit on the throne, and a battle ensued between God and this adversary. He goes by many names: Beelzebub, devil, dragon, the evil one, the god of this age, Leviathan, roaring lion, Satan, serpent, thief, and more.

Where did this angelic jerk come from? When God laid earth’s foundation, his angels shouted for joy, but not all of them offered praise. The most beautiful and powerful of the angels, also named Lucifer, son of the morning, saw the adulation directed toward God and was ticked off, because he thought he deserved some of that glory.

Lucifer incited one-third of the angels to join him in all-out civil war. How did that work out? Not so hot. The Bible calls it a war, but it wasn’t a very exciting one. God basically said, “Lucy, you’re done,” threw him and his buddies out of heaven, and one day, when God decides, will throw him into an eternal fire prepared just for him. That is the backstory of Genesis 3.

documents.excerpt: Genesis 2:9 tells us the Lord made all kinds of trees, pleasing to the eye and good for food, and in the middle of the garden were two special trees: the tree of life and the tree of the knowledge of good and evil.
excerpts: Genesis 2:9 tells us the Lord made all kinds of trees, pleasing to the eye and good for food, and in the middle of the garden were two special trees: the tree of life and the tree of the knowledge of good and evil.

The tree of life was given to sustain us. We were made to live forever; our bodies were designed to reproduce, regenerate, and recreate, so every damaged cell gives way to a newer, healthier one. Cut yourself and white blood cells rush in to heal and drive out infection while red blood cells regenerate new skin. These marvels happen because we were never supposed to die, and the tree of life was God’s gift to ensure living forever would happen.

The tree of the knowledge of good and evil was given to test us. Fancy places tend to have a lot of rules, but the lush garden had only one. God told Adam he was free to eat from any tree, a gazillion of every variety, with one exception: “That tree over there in the middle, you must not eat from that one.” Given the abundance, the command was neither restrictive, harsh, nor controlling. The garden was all about freedom: just don’t mess with that one stinking tree.

documents.excerpt: Satan was a crafty little viper. Instead of saying, “Here, Eve, have a bite,” he plants doubt by mixing a dash of truth with a whole bucket of deception: “Did God really say, ‘You must not eat from any tree in the garden’?” God never said that.
excerpts: Satan was a crafty little viper. Instead of saying, “Here, Eve, have a bite,” he plants doubt by mixing a dash of truth with a whole bucket of deception: “Did God really say, ‘You must not eat from any tree in the garden’?” God never said that.

So Eve springs to the Lord’s defense and answers a question she had no business answering: we can eat from the trees in the garden, but God did say you must not eat fruit from the tree in the middle of the garden, and you must not touch it. Say what? We just read exactly what God said; does he say anything about touching? Like the gecko, Eve misquotes God.
“You will not die,” the serpent said. “For God knows that when you eat of it your eyes will be opened, and you will be like God, knowing good and evil.”

excerpts: She likes it and he likes it until verse 7, when their eyes were opened and they realized they were naked. They had always been naked, but now being naked felt dirty, so they attempt the world’s first cover-up, sewing fig leaves together over their most vulnerable parts.

Then, when they heard the sound of the Lord God walking in the garden, they hid from him among the trees. First they cover up; now they flat out hide. Does that sound familiar? It would be a hoot if it weren’t so tragic: “Quick, Eve, finish your apple, we’ve got to climb this tree,” as though the God who made the tree would be stymied by branches.
We pull the same lame moves. When we do dumb things, we do dumb things to cover them up, and when we feel guilty, we try to hide. So don’t cluck your tongue at Eve. You too. Me too.

Adam and Eve decided to be their own god, and the tragedy that resulted is what we call the fall. Suddenly the human heart wasn’t functioning as designed. documents.context: Steve Wyatt · January 14, 2024 · Genesis
documents.excerpt: We’ve heard “depravity” a lot since the atrocities of October 7. They were utterly depraved; but then again, whose sins aren’t? Total depravity is the evangelical term for the doctrine of original sin, and both are feeble human attempts to describe what happened in the garden that day.
excerpts: We’ve heard “depravity” a lot since the atrocities of October 7. They were utterly depraved; but then again, whose sins aren’t? Total depravity is the evangelical term for the doctrine of original sin, and both are feeble human attempts to describe what happened in the garden that day.

Because of Adam’s sin, the whole human race fell. We were created in God’s image and after his likeness, and we are still image bearers who desire to reverence, trust, obey, and glorify God, but because of Adam’s sin everything changed.

David described it: “Surely I was sinful at birth, and in sin did my mother conceive me.” He isn’t saying it was sinful for his mom to get pregnant and give birth to a precious little shepherd boy, or that he did wrong by being born. He is acknowledging the universal human condition post Genesis 3: all of us are shot through with rebellion, pride, and evil desires, which is why we all fall short of God’s glory again and again.

We are not sinners because we sin; we sin because we are sinners. “Total” doesn’t mean we are as wicked as we could possibly be; it means the fall was so all-encompassing that this global pandemic called sin has infected every heart, and there is no vaccine. According to the apostle Paul our will is in bondage; apart from Jesus we are slaves to sin, and our bodies, minds, and will have been infected.
Is there an antidote? Yes, but slow your roll.

documents.excerpt: Before we go there, we have to go back to the garden, where Adam and Eve are still hiding in the tree. God plays along with their silly game and asks four questions.
excerpts: Before we go there, we have to go back to the garden, where Adam and Eve are still hiding in the tree. God plays along with their silly game and asks four questions.

Question one: “Where are you?” Whom did God ask? The man, not Eve, even though Eve was the first to eat. Centuries later, when Paul teaches about original sin, he doesn’t even mention Eve; he says sin entered the world through one man. Men, being by God’s perfect design the head of your home is not a privilege; it is your solemn responsibility.

God called to the man, “Where are you?” Adam replied, “I heard you in the garden, and I was afraid because I was naked, so I hid.” Question two: “Who told you that you were naked?” Question three: “Did you eat from the tree I commanded you not to eat from?”

documents.excerpt: What happens next is part two of what Steve calls the shame and blame game. Part one, the shame, was the leaf thing. Part two, the blame, is the only somewhat humorous scene in this tragic story, because in less than 13 verses humanity plummets from “Whoa, man, this is bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh” all the way down to “That woman you put with me, she gave it to me. So it’s your fault, God, or hers; you pick. Somebody owes me an apology, and none of this mess is my fault.”

Part two, the blame, is the only somewhat humorous scene in this tragic story, because in less than 13 verses humanity plummets from “Whoa, man, this is bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh” all the way down to “That woman you put with me, she gave it to me. So it’s your fault, God, or hers; you pick. Somebody owes me an apology, and none of this mess is my fault.”

The very first thing the world’s first person did after the first sin was blame God and then his very first wife. Not to be outdone, Eve blames the gecko. After question four, “What is this you have done?”, Eve replies, “It was the serpent. He deceived me.”

Under the weight of shame, the whole cast tries to dodge it by spitting out mutual blame. Sound familiar? Adam was right that Eve played a role, and Eve was right that the serpent lied, but neither was completely right. They both spoke truth, just not the whole truth. Sound familiar?

To the serpent: cursed are you above all the livestock and wild animals; you will crawl on your belly and eat dust all the days of your life. There is more to the snake’s curse, but Steve skips it for now.

Easy, men; this isn’t sexual desire or a desire to please you. It is a sin-corrupted desire. From that moment to this, wives will desire to kick against God’s perfect order for marriage, to rebel, manipulate, and control their man by doing their dead-level best to wrestle away his God-given leadership. Sorry, ladies, Steve is just reporting the news, and if he weren’t straight with them he would be in more serious trouble with someone more powerful than they are.
That is why making a marriage great is so hard: the perfect rhythm God planned for the male-female relationship was already broken 7.2 seconds in.

Making it worse is how men respond, because men botch it too. Insecure enough, with egos fragile enough, we react to our wives’ desire to usurp our leadership in one of two destructive ways. One, men compensate by being bullies, an aggressiveness that can show up verbally, emotionally, and sometimes, God forbid, physically; that is what God predicts in “he will rule over you,” and God didn’t want that either. Two, most men just go passive, hand off the reins, and go watch football, leaving a void that leads to generational brokenness that seems to have no remedy.

excerpts: Turn the page to chapter 4: Adam and Eve are settling into their new digs east of Eden when Eve starts to feel odd, nauseous, out of sorts. Adam, not the brightest crayon, says, “Eve, your garments aren’t fitting like when God gave them to you; are you putting on weight?” Really, dude. Sure enough, she was pregnant and gave birth to Cain, and later to his brother Abel.

With nobody else to play with, you might think the boys got along famously. Not so much. They chose different careers: Abel kept the flocks; Cain worked the fields. And if you picture Abel as the good boy who went to church while Cain bet on camels at the racetrack, drank moonshine, and hated organized religion, not at all. Both were hard workers, both believed in God, and both tried to please him. Cain brought fruits of the soil, and Abel brought fat portions from the firstborn of his flock.

But something was off in Cain’s heart, and God knew it. Why did the Lord look with favor on Abel’s offering but not Cain’s? Hebrews 11:4 unpacks it: Abel offered his sacrifice by faith, but Cain was motivated differently, and we know it because Cain was very angry and his face was downcast.

Why is your face downcast? If you do what is right, will you not be accepted? But if you do not do what is right, sin is crouching at your door; it desires to have you, but you must master it.”
excerpts: God sees it happening to Cain and says something, which is always a great plan. Unlike with Cain’s parents, sin has now become epidemic, so God gets proactive: “Why are you angry? Why is your face downcast? If you do what is right, will you not be accepted? But if you do not do what is right, sin is crouching at your door; it desires to have you, but you must master it.”

“Desires” is the same word God used of Cain’s mom desiring to control his dad. Step one in mastery is recognizing what is happening: “Why are you angry, dude? You think it’s because of Abel, but are you sure he’s the real reason?”

Sin crouches so it can’t clearly be seen, or so it looks smaller and not that big a deal: another deception, like in the garden. “I probably shouldn’t nurse that grudge, but it’s not that bad, not as bad as what he did.” That is a crouching sin you either justify or minimize, and it is still sin.

In the early stages of self-pity, bitterness, pride, greed, anger, even addiction, you still have some measure of control. But a crouching sin creeping slowly and methodically into your life desires to have you and devour you. That jealousy, desire for control, competitiveness: it will have you if you don’t master it, and you’ve got to master it early.

excerpts: We don’t have to end on this tragic note. Remember the leaves Adam and Eve used to cover their shame? It wasn’t long before they started crumbling. Did God say, “That’s what you get”? Laugh at their feeble attempts? Decide it would be easier to make two more of them than clean them up? No.

Because God’s heart is full of redemption, he made them garments of skin and clothed them. In doing so he painted a picture of his heart of forgiveness and what it would cost: a covering of animal skin required that blood be shed, pointing ahead to a coming Savior who would lay down his life and purchase salvation for a lost, broken world. God painted that picture and promised he would pay the price, right then, right there.

documents.context: Josh Wyatt · January 7, 2024 · Genesis
documents.excerpt: Moses wrote Genesis, part of the Pentateuch, the first five books of the Hebrew Bible. A massive question is answered in just its first couple of verses: who is God?
excerpts: Moses wrote Genesis, part of the Pentateuch, the first five books of the Hebrew Bible. A massive question is answered in just its first couple of verses: who is God?

Notice what the question isn’t. There is no proof of God in Genesis 1 and no apologetic approach; Moses simply assumes God exists and that it is foolish to assume otherwise. Genesis is all about God, all of history is about God, science is about God; there is simply a proclamation of his existence and presence: “In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth.”

This is an ancient text, roughly three and a half thousand years old. Ideas, philosophies, religions, and trends have come and gone, and Genesis still remains. It is a great place to learn about God, but reader beware: it isn’t exhaustive. From chapter 1 to chapter 50 Moses covers about 2,000 years of human history, about as much as the rest of the Bible combined. It gives us what we need to sufficiently answer the question, who is God?

documents.context: Josh Wyatt · January 7, 2024 · Genesis
documents.excerpt: We can’t really argue the creation question one way or another, because none of us was there to see it go down. Besides common sense, verse 2 says the earth was formless and empty, with darkness over the deep and the Spirit of God hovering over the waters.
excerpts: We can’t really argue the creation question one way or another, because none of us was there to see it go down. Besides common sense, verse 2 says the earth was formless and empty, with darkness over the deep and the Spirit of God hovering over the waters.

We can hypothesize through science and philosophy, but the only way to truly know what happened is not by guessing but by being told: by revelation. The only one there was God, so he tells the story only he can tell. Hebrews 11 says by faith we understand that the universe was formed at God’s command.

The origin of the universe has yet to be explained apart from faith. After centuries of speculation, people keep sharing notes and get no closer. Josh read quote after quote this week from scientists and philosophers at the end of their lives, and all he saw was frustration. Bertrand Russell wrote that we must conquer the world by intelligence, but if you can’t determine how it started, how do you intend to conquer it?
Josh takes it by faith that the universe was formed at God’s command; they take it by faith that it began by accident. Where do you stand?

documents.title: Hollow and deceptive philosophy — Who is God?

Questions flow immediately from “in the beginning”: when was that, and how old is the earth? Josh polls the room: who thinks it is 4.5 billion years old, who thinks six to 10,000 years, and who won’t raise a hand for fear of getting jumped by their small group leader in the lobby.

Christians love to debate this, and Josh doesn’t know why, since the very next phrase literally says God created the heavens and the earth. God speaks and suddenly void becomes vibrant, and leave it to us to argue about how old it is. The Hebrew word for beginning means begin, first; it doesn’t say how old the earth is. God says, “I made it”; we say, “I must know when.” If God wanted you to know, wouldn’t he have told you?

In those conversations Josh figures out what the other person thinks and agrees fast so the conversation can be over. Old or young, he doesn’t care; he is glad you are here to worship and call him king.

The Hebrew word here, bara, means to bring into existence. God brought the earth into existence and set it up so we could move in, live here, and enjoy him and what he worked for. Cleaning the pool a few months ago he found a living frog; his wife, with her big heart, demanded it be set free, not murdered, and said, “Handle it.” He tried to fling it over the wall with the dustpan, misjudged the trajectory, and the frog slammed into the wall to certain and immediate death. documents.context: Josh Wyatt · January 7, 2024 · Genesis
documents.excerpt: Within the last 20 years scientists have discovered that the universe has been precisely tweaked to support life; change almost anything by the smallest increment and we would cease to exist. If gravity, the force wrecking your knees and joints, were altered by more than one part in 10 to the 40th power, stars wouldn’t exist, and neither would we.
excerpts: Within the last 20 years scientists have discovered that the universe has been precisely tweaked to support life; change almost anything by the smallest increment and we would cease to exist. If gravity, the force wrecking your knees and joints, were altered by more than one part in 10 to the 40th power, stars wouldn’t exist, and neither would we.

Josh shares Frank Turek’s illustration: stretch a tape measure across the entire known universe and set gravity at one inch mark. If it were different by one inch in either direction across a scale as wide as the universe, we wouldn’t be here.

Are we supposed to believe our planet just won the cosmic lottery? Third from the sun, in the Goldilocks zone: a little closer and we’d burn, a little farther and we’d freeze. Change the 23.5-degree axial tilt, the 24-hour rotation, or the size and distance of the moon slightly, and we don’t exist. His favorite: if Jupiter doesn’t hold orbit, we don’t exist. Without Jupiter and Saturn we’d need Bruce Willis from Armageddon blowing up asteroids every week.
The average distance between stars in our galaxy, about 30 trillion miles, is required for life on earth, and the stars are as many as the grains of sand on all the beaches on the planet.

Homework: read the entire chapter of Isaiah 40. Isaiah is writing to a nation in turmoil and saying God’s got this; look at God’s sovereignty. So who is God? Instead of turning on Netflix tonight, go out and look up and get an education there.

documents.context: Josh Wyatt · January 7, 2024 · Genesis
documents.excerpt: God said, “Let there be light,” and there was light; he separated light from darkness, and there was evening and morning, the first day.
excerpts: God said, “Let there be light,” and there was light; he separated light from darkness, and there was evening and morning, the first day.

Josh believes these are literal days. He can’t start thinking the Bible says stuff it never says; he remembers somebody doing that in Genesis 3, and it didn’t go well. Scripture seems clear: Exodus 20 says in six days the Lord made the heavens and the earth, the sea, and all that is in them, but rested on the seventh day, and blessed the Sabbath and made it holy.

God speaks and creation listens; that is the theme of Genesis 1. It was dark, God spoke, and the sun rises. Don’t miss this: God speaks every day. He is involved in every sunrise and sunset. Do you wake up thinking, “God, you’re the master architect; you’ve done it again,” or do you think he set everything in motion and is taking a divine cosmic nap until the day of the Lord? The rising of the sun is the work of his hand.

documents.excerpt: God made two great lights, the greater to govern the day and the lesser to govern the night, and the stars, to mark seasons, days, and years and to separate light from darkness; the fourth day.
excerpts: God made two great lights, the greater to govern the day and the lesser to govern the night, and the stars, to mark seasons, days, and years and to separate light from darkness; the fourth day.

Another debate, and Josh excuses his frustration, since God creates the universe from nothing and we turn it into foolish debate: when did God make the sun? Verse 1, day one with “let there be light,” or day four? Josh doesn’t think day four is when God literally created the sun but when he announced it. None of it matters much to him; all he sees is God sorting the cosmos like Josh sorts his son’s Legos. He doesn’t have questions to ask; he has songs to sing.
Maybe God needs to announce his creation, so that people worshiping the stars find out God made them and say, “Our bad, we’ll just worship you and skip the middleman.”

God cares about your quality of life. He wants you to sleep well and enjoy your day; he cares that you have time to work and to rest, to be with your spouse, kids, and grandkids. Far too many see God as a cruel overlord, but even despite our arrogance and rebellion he is gracious, kind, loving, and generous.

documents.context: Josh Wyatt · January 7, 2024 · Genesis
documents.excerpt: Day five has Discovery Channel written all over it: the waters teem with living creatures, birds fly across the sky, and God blesses them to be fruitful and increase; the fifth day.
excerpts: Day five has Discovery Channel written all over it: the waters teem with living creatures, birds fly across the sky, and God blesses them to be fruitful and increase; the fifth day.
Did you catch verse 22? God blessed them: the animals. Genesis talks about God pouring out blessing more than any other book in the Bible, over 80 times: God blessed, I will bless you.
So who is God? He is the uncaused causer, he is good, and he desires to bless you. If he rolls out blessings to the animals, how much more will he offer you?

documents.context: Josh Wyatt · January 7, 2024 · Genesis
documents.excerpt: Josh bets many, like him, have struggled with self-worth: things they don’t like about themselves, or things others would change. This week he accidentally shaved off his goatee, and when his wife saw him, her face said, “What have you done to my husband?” Laughing about it, he realized we all struggle with our image and our insecurities in different ways.
excerpts: Josh bets many, like him, have struggled with self-worth: things they don’t like about themselves, or things others would change. This week he accidentally shaved off his goatee, and when his wife saw him, her face said, “What have you done to my husband?” Laughing about it, he realized we all struggle with our image and our insecurities in different ways.
The truth is that God is pleased with how he made you. He made each of us for a reason, with a God-given purpose; you have value because he assigned you value.
We went and made a mess of things, and our hearts were deceived, but the image we bear is still his. We don’t wear that with the honor we should. We are his; we belong to him; we were bought.

documents.context: Josh Wyatt · January 7, 2024 · Genesis
documents.excerpt: A lot of us don’t take time to rest; we’re bad at it. In chapter 2 Moses says the heavens and the earth were completed, and on the seventh day God rested from all his work, blessed the seventh day, and made it holy.
excerpts: A lot of us don’t take time to rest; we’re bad at it. In chapter 2 Moses says the heavens and the earth were completed, and on the seventh day God rested from all his work, blessed the seventh day, and made it holy.

If God chooses to rest, you should too. Many rob themselves of joy and vitality by refusing to slow down or take a break, but God sets the example. We are blessed when we create, but we are blessed when we rest.
Genesis 2 continues with another account of creation; read it before next week. The homework: Isaiah 40, Romans 11, and Genesis 2. A busy week, but you can handle it.

documents.context: Josh Wyatt · January 7, 2024 · Genesis
documents.excerpt: Josh prays as the church heads into communion, the Lord’s Supper, a time of fellowship with God to remember what he did, approached with reverence. He wants to be like Jesus, who walked through tightly gathered crowds and paused and stopped when a sick woman who believed in him reached out and touched him; he asks God to show him when to pause and stop, and whom to care for and love so they can know him.
excerpts: Josh prays as the church heads into communion, the Lord’s Supper, a time of fellowship with God to remember what he did, approached with reverence. He wants to be like Jesus, who walked through tightly gathered crowds and paused and stopped when a sick woman who believed in him reached out and touched him; he asks God to show him when to pause and stop, and whom to care for and love so they can know him.

He thinks of the Last Supper and the patience and love that let a betrayer sit in the room, and asks not to be shaken by the betrayers in his life. Either God is sovereign or he isn’t; Josh believes he is in absolute control, so when God takes something, he doesn’t ask where God was but what he is working on.

He prays to be like the Son in the garden, about to carry the load of our sin and pay our debt in full, asking for a strong back to carry others as Jesus carried him, and to be faithful when all alone, as Jesus was on the cross. “You spoke it into existence and it is good.” He thanks God for loving, providing for, and saving him.
